definition_en: for that reason; used to introduce a conclusion drawn from what has just been said
core_image: 两段链条扣在一起，前一段的末端正好接上后一段的起点
scene: 报告的最后一页列出了全部数据，结论顺理成章地跟着出现。 The pass was closed by snow; therefore the convoy took the longer road.
sceneCN: 这里 therefore 是「因此、所以」（第 1 个义项：表示由前文推出的结论）；句意给出由数据推出结论的典型场景。

pos.zh: 因此；所以；故（连接性副词，引出由前文推出的结论）

derivatives.zh: 借此；由此（同构复合词，fore 换成 by）
为此（法律用语，与 therefore 的构词成分相同）
为何；原因（where + fore 的同构形式）

senses.title: For that reason
senses.definition: used to introduce a result that the previous statement provides the reason for
senses.definitionCN: 引出结果，而前面的陈述给出这一结果的理由
senses.example: The road was closed; therefore we took the longer route.
senses.exampleCN: 道路封闭了，因此我们走了更远的那条路。
senses.why: Therefore is there plus fore, for that: the word points back at the stated cause and presents what follows as owed to it.
senses.whyCN: therefore 是 there 加 fore「为此」：它回指已说出的原因，并把后文呈现为由那个原因所欠下的。

senses.title: The inevitable step in an argument
senses.titleCN: 论证中必然推出的结论
senses.definition: used in logic where the conclusion cannot be false if the premises are true
senses.definitionCN: 用于逻辑，当前提为真时结论不可能为假
senses.example: All men are mortal; Socrates is a man; therefore Socrates is mortal.
senses.exampleCN: 人皆有死；苏格拉底是人；因此苏格拉底有死。
senses.why: In a syllogism the word marks the forced last line, the point at which the premises hand over their conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 在三段论里，这个词标出被迫写下的最后一行，也就是前提交出结论的那一点。

senses.title: The conclusion of a proof
senses.definition: used in mathematics to introduce a result derived from earlier steps
senses.definitionCN: 数学中用于引出由前面步骤得到的结果
senses.example: The two triangles are congruent; therefore their angles are equal.
senses.exampleCN: 两个三角形全等，因此它们的角相等。
senses.why: Proof writing needs a visible hinge between the derivation and the result, and this is that hinge.
senses.whyCN: 证明写作需要在推导与结果之间有一个看得见的铰链，这个词就是那个铰链。

senses.title: The formal hence of legal prose
senses.definition: used in formal and legal writing to state a required consequence
senses.definitionCN: 在正式与法律文字中陈述必须产生的后果
senses.example: The defendant failed to appear; therefore the court proceeded.
senses.exampleCN: 被告未出庭，故法庭继续审理。
senses.why: Statutes chain a condition to a consequence, and the older register of the word suits that chain of obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法条把条件与后果串起来，而这个词较古的语体正适合这条义务链。

senses.title: For that purpose, in older English
senses.definition: archaic: for that purpose or to that end
senses.definitionCN: 古旧义：为了那个目的、朝向那个目标
senses.example: He laboured therefore that the work might be finished.
senses.exampleCN: 他为此辛勤劳作，好把那件工作完成。
senses.why: Fore once meant for or on account of, so the compound could carry purpose as well as cause; modern English keeps mainly the causal sense.
senses.whyCN: fore 旧有「为了、由于」之义，因此这个复合词既能表目的也能表原因；现代英语主要保留因果义。

senses.title: The close of a rebuttal
senses.definition: used to close an argument after the evidence has been weighed
senses.definitionCN: 在证据权衡完毕后用来收束论证
senses.example: The evidence is incomplete; therefore the claim cannot stand.
senses.exampleCN: 证据不完整，因此这一主张不能成立。
senses.why: Debate ends by naming what the audience must accept, and the word converts a review of evidence into a verdict.
senses.whyCN: 辩论以点明听众必须接受什么来收尾，这个词把对证据的回顾转成裁决。

senses.title: The inference in an experiment
senses.definition: used in reports to state what the data allow the authors to infer
senses.definitionCN: 在报告中陈述数据让作者能推出什么
senses.example: The readings were consistent; therefore the model was accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 读数一致，因此该模型被接受。
senses.why: Scientific style separates observation from inference, and the word marks the crossing point.
senses.whyCN: 科学文体把观察与推论分开，这个词标出跨越的那一点。

senses.title: The summing up in teaching
senses.definition: used in explanation to gather the previous points into one conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 在讲解中把前面的要点收拢成一个结论
senses.example: Therefore, the plan needs revision before the next stage.
senses.exampleCN: 因此，这项计划在进入下一阶段之前需要修订。
senses.why: Teaching needs a marker that says the scattered facts now add up, which is the conversational use of the same hinge.
senses.whyCN: 教学需要一个标记说「零散的事实到此合成一个结论」，这是同一个铰链的口语用法。

intro.en: Therefore is an English compound of there and fore, an old word for before or for that. It is Germanic, not Latin, and the Latin ergo is a counterpart rather than a source. The direct source is clear; the first date is approximate.
intro.cn: therefore 是英语复合词，由 there 与 fore 构成，fore 是表示「在前、为此」的古词。它属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，拉丁语 ergo 只是对应词而非来源。直接来源清楚，首见年代为约数。

items.en: There comes from Old English thær, the locative form meaning in that place, later extended to that point in speech.
items.cn: there 来自古英语 thær，本为「在那个地方」的处所形式，后来扩展到言语中的「那一点」。

items.en: Fore meant before or in front, and in phrases it could mean for that or on account of that.
items.cn: fore 意为在前，在短语中也可表「为了那个、由于那个」。

items.en: The two parts join as therfore in the Middle English period, keeping the pointing function of there.
items.cn: 两部分在中古英语时期合为 therfore，保留了 there 的回指功能。

items.en: Sixteenth-century prose fixes therefore as the standard marker of a conclusion, beside the older thus and hence.
items.cn: 十六世纪的印本散文把 therefore 固定为结论标记，与较早的 thus、hence 并列。

items.en: Modern English keeps therefore for logical consequence and therefor, a different spelling, for legal purpose.
items.cn: 现代英语用 therefore 表逻辑后果，而用拼写不同的 therefor 表法律上的目的。

note.en: The first group shares the there plus fore pattern and includes the look-alike therefor. The second group names conclusions and reasons, and includes consequently and subsequently, which differ in whether causation is claimed.
note.cn: 第一组共享 there + fore 的构词模式，并包含形近的 therefor。第二组表示结论与理由，其中 consequently 与 subsequently 的区别在于是否主张因果。

entries.definition: For that purpose, a legal spelling with one r fewer than therefore; it is not a misspelling of the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 为此目的，法律用语，比 therefore 少一个 r；它不是 therefore 的拼写错误。

entries.definition: By that means, with by in place of fore.
entries.definitionCN: 借此、由此，用 by 代替 fore。

entries.definition: Of that or of it, in legal and formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 其、由此，用于法律与正式文字。

entries.definition: In that place or in that document.
entries.definitionCN: 在其中、在该文件之内。

entries.definition: For what reason, built on where instead of there, and preserved in legal and poetic prose.
entries.definitionCN: 为何、由于什么，用 where 而非 there 构成，存于法律与诗歌文字中。

entries.definition: In this way or as a result, often marking a conclusion in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 如此、因此，正式文字中常作结论标记。

entries.definition: From this fact, as a consequence; also from this time.
entries.definitionCN: 由此、因此；也表「从此时起」。

entries.definition: As a result; stronger on causation and weaker on argument than therefore.
entries.definitionCN: 结果上；比 therefore 更强调因果，论证色彩较弱。

entries.definition: In a way that matches what has just been said, often of action taken.
entries.definitionCN: 按照刚说的情况而行事。

entries.definition: Afterwards in time only; it never supplies the causal link that therefore carries.
entries.definitionCN: 只表时间上的随后；它从不提供 therefore 所带的因果连接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real there plus fore pattern and keep therefore apart from subsequently and consequently.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 there + fore 构词模式，并把 therefore 与 subsequently、consequently 区分开。

normal.en: There points back, fore means for: therefore is for that, pointing at the reason just given.
normal.cn: there 回指，fore 意为「为了」：therefore 就是「为此」，指向刚给出的理由。

normal.en: In a syllogism the word is the last line, the place where premises hand over their conclusion.
normal.cn: 在三段论里，这个词是最后一行，是前提交出结论的地方。

normal.en: Mathematicians write therefore where the proof turns from work to result.
normal.cn: 数学家在证明从推导转向结果的地方写 therefore。

normal.en: Then there is time, therefore is cause: one is a clock, the other a hinge.
normal.cn: then 是时间，therefore 是原因：一个是钟，一个是铰链。

normal.en: Lawyers keep therefor with one r for purpose, and therefore with two for conclusions.
normal.cn: 律师用少一个 r 的 therefor 表目的，用两个 r 的 therefore 表结论。

abstract.en: A conclusion is a debt the earlier sentence has already agreed to pay.
abstract.cn: 结论是前一句话已经答应偿付的一笔债。

abstract.en: Saying therefore is claiming that nothing else could have followed.
abstract.cn: 说「因此」，就是在主张不可能有别的结果。

abstract.en: The word works because two sentences can be made to touch.
abstract.cn: 这个词能起作用，只因为两句话可以被接得贴在一起。

examples.en: The sample was contaminated; therefore the results were discarded.
examples.cn: 样品被污染，因此结果作废。

examples.en: The two accounts disagree; therefore at least one is wrong.
examples.cn: 两种说法互相矛盾，因此至少有一种是错的。

examples.en: The bridge carries no traffic; therefore repairs can wait.
examples.cn: 这座桥不通车，因此修缮可以推迟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「戴尔福」，there 指「那件事」，fore 指「为了」：为了那件事，所以如此

root: 英语复合词 there + fore（fore 古义为「在前、为了」）。属日耳曼语来源，拉丁语 ergo「因此」只是对应词而非词源，故不列拉丁同族。现代英语用 therefore 表逻辑后果，用拼写 therefor 表法律上的目的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one hinge: something has been stated, and what follows is presented as owed to it. The setting changes from daily reasoning to syllogism, proof, statute, archaic purpose, rebuttal, experiment and classroom summary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个铰链：某事已被陈述，后文被呈现为由它欠下的。场景从日常推理换到三段论、证明、法条、古旧的目的义、辩驳、实验与课堂总结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chains joined so that the end of one meets the beginning of the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条链条相接，前一条的末端正好扣住后一条的起点。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY CAUSE: a result the previous sentence has already paid for.
branches.cn: 日常原因：前一语句已经付过账的结果。

branches.en: THE FORCED LINE: the last step of a syllogism, and the closing line of a proof.
branches.cn: 被迫的一行：三段论的最后一步，以及证明的收束句。

branches.en: THE STATUTE: a condition in law handing over a required consequence.
branches.cn: 法条：法律中的条件交出必须承担的后果。

branches.en: THE OLD PURPOSE: for that end, a sense modern English has mostly dropped.
branches.cn: 古旧目的义：为了那个目标，现代英语已大体舍弃。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: closing a rebuttal, crossing from data to inference, and summing up a lesson.
branches.cn: 裁决：收束辩驳、从数据跨到推论，以及总结一堂课。

intro.en: Therefore is not a suffixed word but a compound of there and fore. English reuses the same frame in thereby, therein, thereof and the legal therefor, and wherefore swaps where for there.
intro.cn: therefore 不是加后缀的词，而是 there 与 fore 的复合词。英语用同一框架造出 thereby、therein、thereof 与法律用语的 therefor，wherefore 则把 where 换到 there 的位置。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so no Latin entries are listed. Latin ergo and igitur are counterparts in meaning only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。拉丁语 ergo 与 igitur 只是在意义上对应。

items.meaning: in that place; at that point
items.meaningCN: 在那个地方；在那一点上
items.example: The first half of the compound is the pointing finger.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半截就是那根指过去的手指。

items.example: The second half supplies the sense of on account of.
items.exampleCN: 后半截提供「由于、为了」的意思。

items.example: The compound is fixed by the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词在十六世纪固定下来。

items.example: Legal drafters keep the shorter spelling for purpose.
items.exampleCN: 法律起草者用较短的拼写表目的。

items.example: The frame swaps fore for by and keeps the pointing.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架把 fore 换成 by，回指功能不变。

items.example: The same slot also takes a preposition of place.
items.exampleCN: 同一个位置也可以放表示处所的前置词。

items.example: Contracts use the form to point back at a defined item.
items.exampleCN: 合同用它回指已定义的事项。

items.example: The interrogative version of the same frame survives in legal prose.
items.exampleCN: 同一框架的疑问版本存活于法律文字中。

items.example: It is the older rival that therefore largely displaced.
items.exampleCN: 它是 therefore 大体上取代了的较早对手。

items.example: It marks manner as well as conclusion, which therefore does not.
items.exampleCN: 它既标方式也标结论，而 therefore 不标方式。

definition_en: to catch a person or animal, or to take control of a place by force
core_image: 伸手把正在奔跑的东西一把抓住
scene: 警察当天就抓获了那名小偷。 The police captured the thief the same day.
sceneCN: 这里 captured 是 capture 的过去式，意为「抓获」（第 1 个义项：把人或动物抓住）；句意是警察当天就抓住了那名小偷。

derivatives.zh: 与 capture 同根，义为「被俘虏的；被关起来的」
captive 加 -ity 构成，义为「囚禁状态」
由同一词根加 -or 构成，义为「捕获者、抓人的人」

senses.title: To catch a person or animal
senses.definition: to take a person or animal prisoner by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力把人或动物抓住并控制住
senses.example: Soldiers captured three scouts near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵在河边抓获了三名侦察兵。
senses.why: Latin capere means to seize, and capture keeps that physical action of grabbing hold.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capere 意为「抓住」，capture 保留了抓住东西这一身体动作。

senses.title: To take control of a place
senses.definition: to seize a place or thing by force, especially in war
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指在战争中用武力夺取一个地方或物品
senses.example: The army captured the city after a long siege.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长期围困，军队攻占了这座城市。
senses.why: Taking a city is the same gesture as taking a prisoner, only the object is larger.
senses.whyCN: 攻下一座城与抓住一个人是同一个动作，只是对象变大了。

senses.title: To record or hold attention
senses.definition: to record an image, sound, or feeling, or to hold someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 把影像、声音或感受记录下来，或牢牢吸引住某人的注意
senses.example: The photograph captures the light of that morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这张照片捕捉到了那个早晨的光。
senses.why: A camera takes hold of a moment the way a hand takes hold of an object.
senses.whyCN: 相机「抓住」一个瞬间，正如手抓住一件物品，于是有了「捕捉影像」的义项。

intro.en: Capture comes straight from the Latin verb for seizing, by way of a noun meaning a taking.
intro.cn: capture 直接来自拉丁语中表示「抓取」的动词，经由一个意为「拿取」的名词进入英语。

items.en: capere meant to take, seize, or hold, and it is the root behind cap- and capt-.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、抓、控制」，是 cap- 与 capt- 词根的来源。

items.en: captura named a taking or a catch, especially of animals.
items.cn: captura 指「拿取、捕获」，尤其指猎获动物。

items.en: Old French capture kept the legal and military sense of taking a person or place.
items.cn: 古法语 capture 保留了夺取人或地方的法律与军事含义。

items.en: English borrowed capture for the act of taking a prisoner or a town.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 capture，指俘获俘虏或攻占城镇。

items.en: Photography and computing extended it to recording images, sound, and data.
items.cn: 摄影与计算机技术把它的词义扩展到记录影像、声音和数据。

note.en: Capture belongs to the Latin family of seizing, and its near meanings all involve taking hold.
note.cn: capture 属于拉丁语「抓取」词族，近义词都与「抓住」有关。

entries.definition: kept as a prisoner
entries.definitionCN: 被俘虏的、被关押的，与 capture 同根。

entries.definition: a person who captures someone
entries.definitionCN: 捕获者、抓人的人，由同一词根加 -or 构成。

entries.definition: to hold someone's attention completely
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷，字面意思是「把人抓住」。

entries.definition: to take hold of something suddenly and by force
entries.definitionCN: 突然用力抓住某物，最贴近 capture 的动作义。

entries.definition: to take someone into legal custody
entries.definitionCN: 依法逮捕某人，对应「抓获」义。

entries.definition: to take something quickly and roughly
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而粗鲁地抓住，是口语说法。

normalIntro.en: The root capt- means seized, and every sense is a version of taking hold.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 capt- 意为「被抓住」，每个义项都是「抓住」的一种版本。

normal.en: capt- comes from Latin capere, to seize, the same root as captive and captor.
normal.cn: capt- 来自拉丁语 capere（抓取），与 captive、captor 同根。

normal.en: A prisoner is captured, and so is a city: the verb does not change.
normal.cn: 俘虏可以被 capture，城市也可以被 capture，动词本身不变。

normal.en: capture the attention treats attention as something that can be grabbed.
normal.cn: capture the attention 把注意力当成可以抓走的东西。

normal.en: A camera captures a moment, which links photography with the same old verb.
normal.cn: 相机 capture 一个瞬间，把摄影和这个古老动词连在一起。

normal.en: The noun capture is simply the act: the capture of the town.
normal.cn: 名词 capture 就是那个动作本身：攻占该镇。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a bird that was about to fly away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手合拢，抓住一只正要飞走的鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a flag being pulled down and another raised in its place.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗被拉下，另一面旗在原地升起。

abstract.en: Picture a camera shutter closing on one second of light.
abstract.cn: 想象相机快门合拢，把一秒的光收进去。

examples.en: The police captured the thief the same day.
examples.cn: 警察当天就抓获了那名小偷。

examples.en: The army captured the city after a long siege.
examples.cn: 经过长期围困，军队攻占了这座城市。

examples.en: The photograph captures the light of that morning.
examples.cn: 这张照片捕捉到了那个早晨的光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普车」——开车追上去，一把把人抓住。

root: 拉丁语 capere（抓住、夺取）→ captura（捕获）→ 古法语 capture → 英语 capture。

sensesIntro.en: One gesture of seizing runs through all senses, from prisoners to cities to photographs.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「抓住」的动作贯穿全部义项，从俘虏到城市再到照片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing around something that is trying to get away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢，抓住正想逃走的东西。

branches.en: The personal sense: taking a person or animal prisoner.
branches.cn: 指人的义项：把人或动物抓为俘虏。

branches.en: The territorial sense: taking a city or position by force.
branches.cn: 指地域的义项：用武力攻占城市或阵地。

branches.en: The recording sense: taking an image, sound, or feeling into a device.
branches.cn: 记录义：把影像、声音或感受收进设备里。

branches.en: Both older senses share the idea of force against a resisting object.
branches.cn: 两个较早的义项都共享「以武力对付抵抗者」的意思。

branches.en: The modern sense softens force into attention: a good story captures listeners.
branches.cn: 现代义把「武力」软化为「吸引力」：好故事能抓住听众。

intro.en: Capture is built on the root capt-, seized, with the noun and verb ending -ure.
intro.cn: capture 建立在词根 capt-（被抓住的）上，加上名词兼动词词尾 -ure。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere and captura give English capture, captive, and captor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 与 captura 给英语带来 capture、captive、captor 等词。

items.example: They captured the moment on film.
items.exampleCN: 他们用胶片记录下那个瞬间。

items.meaning: he, she, or it seizes something
items.example: The novel captures village life well.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说很好地捕捉了乡村生活。

items.meaning: seized or recorded in the past
items.example: The rebels captured the radio station.

items.meaning: the act of seizing or recording
items.example: The team is capturing images of the coast.
items.exampleCN: 团队正在拍摄海岸影像。

items.example: The captive birds were later released.
items.exampleCN: 被关的鸟后来被放生了。

items.meaning: the state of being held prisoner

items.exampleCN: 劫持者未伤司机便将其释放。

definition_en: one of the parts into which something is divided, a department, a part of a book, or a cut-away view
core_image: 厚书摊开在桌上，书签夹在标着章节号的那一页
scene: 他翻到讲方法的章节，用铅笔在页边画了个圈。 She turned to the section on methods.
sceneCN: 这里 section 是「章节」（第 3 个义项）；句意：她翻到讲方法的那一节。

senses.title: One of the parts
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a whole is divided
senses.definitionCN: 整体被分成的部分之一
senses.example: This section of the road is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 这段路封闭了。
senses.why: This is the broad physical sense.

senses.title: A department
senses.definition: a separate part of an organization or shop
senses.definitionCN: 组织或商店中独立的部门
senses.example: She works in the sports section.
senses.exampleCN: 她在体育部工作。
senses.why: Organizations divide work into sections.
senses.whyCN: 组织把工作分成各个部门。

senses.title: A part of a book
senses.definition: a part of a book, report, or newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 书、报告或报纸中的一个部分
senses.example: Read the first section of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 读报告的第一节。
senses.why: Written works are divided into sections.
senses.whyCN: 文字作品被分成章节。

senses.title: A cut-away view
senses.definition: a view of something as if cut through
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛被切开后看到的样子
senses.example: The diagram shows a cross section of the pipe.

intro.en: Section comes from Latin sectio, a cutting, from secare, to cut.
intro.cn: section 源自拉丁语 sectio（切割），出自 secare（切）。

items.en: Secare meant to cut.
items.cn: secare 意为切。

items.en: Sectio meant a cutting or a piece cut off.
items.cn: sectio 意为切割或切下的部分。

items.en: Section entered English as a part cut from a whole.
items.cn: section 以「从整体切下的部分」进入英语。

items.en: Books and organizations began to use sections.
items.cn: 书籍与组织开始使用 section 划分。

items.en: The word also names a technical cross-section.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也指技术性的横截面。

note.en: Section is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts.
note.cn: 把 section 与形近词以及表示部分的词作比较。

entries.definition: a part of an economy or a pie slice
entries.definitionCN: 部门；扇形

entries.definition: a period of activity or meeting
entries.definitionCN: 会议；时段

entries.definition: the act of choosing
entries.definitionCN: 选择

entries.definition: a piece of a whole

entries.definition: a part of an organization
entries.definitionCN: 部门；划分

entries.definition: one of several parts

normalIntro.en: A section is a part cut from a whole, whether a road, a shop, a book, or a pipe.
normalIntro.cn: section 是从整体切下的一部分，无论是道路、商店、书还是管道。

normal.en: Section and sector both come from a root meaning to cut.
normal.cn: section 与 sector 都出自表示「切」的词根。

normal.en: A newspaper has a sports section and a business section.
normal.cn: 报纸有体育版和商业版。

normal.en: Read the report section by section.
normal.cn: 要一部分一部分地读报告。

normal.en: A cross section shows the inside of an object.
normal.cn: 横截面展示物体内部。

normal.en: A subsection is a smaller section inside one.
normal.cn: subsection 是章节内更小的节。

abstract.en: To understand a whole, we cut it into sections.
abstract.cn: 为了理解整体，我们把它切成部分。

abstract.en: Every section belongs to something larger.
abstract.cn: 每个部分都属于某个更大的整体。

abstract.en: A cross section reveals what the surface hides.
abstract.cn: 横截面揭示表面所隐藏的东西。

examples.en: This section of the road is closed.
examples.cn: 这段路封闭了。

examples.en: She works in the sports section.
examples.cn: 她在体育部工作。

examples.en: Read the first section of the report.
examples.cn: 读报告的第一节。

root: 源自拉丁语 sectio（切割），出自 secare（切），核心义「从整体切分出的部分」。

core.en: A piece separated from a larger whole.

branches.cn: 文本中编号的一部分。

branches.en: Every section is literally a kind of cut.

intro.en: Section forms words for divisions, smaller parts, and cut-away views.
intro.cn: section 构成表示划分、更小部分与剖面视图的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sectio and secare are the historical sources.

definition_zh: 网站；网页集合；（一个域下的）站点
definition_en: a set of connected pages on the internet, usually belonging to one person or organisation
core_image: 一张网把许多房间连起来，每个房间门口挂着一块招牌
scene: 小书店的柜台旁贴着二维码，顾客扫开就能看到全部书目。 The bookshop's website lists every title it has in stock.
sceneCN: 这里 website 是「网站」（第 1 个义项：互联网上相互连接的一系列页面）；句意为这家书店的网站列出了所有库存书目。门上挂招牌的连片房间，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 截短形式，义为「站点；场地」
复合词，义为「网站管理员」
本词的第一部分，义为「网；万维网」

senses.title: A set of connected pages
senses.titleCN: 网站：互相链接的一组页面
senses.definition: a group of connected pages on the internet that share one address
senses.definitionCN: 互联网上共用同一地址、彼此相连的一组页面
senses.example: The museum's website has a virtual tour of every hall.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的网站上有每个展厅的虚拟导览。
senses.why: web names the linking and site names the place; a website is a place built out of links.
senses.whyCN: web 指相互连接，site 指地点；website 就是由链接搭成的一个地方。

senses.title: An organisation's online home
senses.titleCN: 机构网站：组织在网络上的门面
senses.definition: the online presence of a company, school or public body, where information is published
senses.definitionCN: 公司、学校或公共机构在网络上发布信息的所在
senses.example: Apply through the university website before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 请在截止日期之前通过大学网站申请。
senses.why: A site is a plot of ground; the digital plot is where an organisation keeps its public face.
senses.whyCN: site 本是一块地；数字的「地」就是机构摆放门面的地方。

senses.title: A commercial shop online
senses.titleCN: 网上店铺：可下单选购的站点
senses.definition: a website used for selling goods or services, with pages for browsing and buying
senses.definitionCN: 用于出售商品或服务、可浏览下单的网站
senses.example: Their website takes orders until midnight and ships the next day.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的网站接单到午夜，第二天发货。
senses.why: The site turns into a counter: browsing pages leads to a basket and a payment, and the ground becomes a shop floor.
senses.whyCN: 站点变成了柜台：浏览页面通向购物篮与付款，那块「地」也就成了店面。

senses.title: One address, many pages
senses.titleCN: 一个地址下的整个站点
senses.definition: used of the whole collection of pages under a single domain name
senses.definitionCN: 指单一域名下的全部页面集合
senses.example: The old website is still online, though no one updates it.
senses.exampleCN: 旧网站仍然在线，尽管已经没人更新了。
senses.why: The plural pages are gathered under one name, and that name is the website as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 众多页面被收在一个名字之下，那个名字就是作为整体的网站。

senses.title: As a shortened form
senses.definition: in everyday speech often shortened to site, especially with a modifier
senses.definitionCN: 口语中常简写为 site，尤与修饰语连用
senses.example: Check the site for the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 去网站上看新的时间表。
senses.why: Speech shortens what print once spelled in two words, and site alone carries the whole meaning in context.
senses.whyCN: 口语把书面曾用两个词写的东西缩短，而 site 单用在语境中已含全部意思。

intro.en: Website is a late twentieth-century compound of web, from Old English, and site, from Latin.
intro.cn: website 是二十世纪后期的复合词，由古英语的 web 与拉丁语的 site 合成。

items.en: Web meant a woven cloth, and later the net of a spider; the sense of connected links came naturally.
items.cn: web 原指织成的布，后指蛛网；由此自然生出「相互链接」之义。

items.en: Situs meant 'a position, a site', from sinere 'to let, to place'; English site came through French.
items.cn: situs 意为「位置、地点」，出自 sinere「放置」；英语 site 经法语而来。

items.en: The World Wide Web was named at CERN around 1989, and web was quickly applied to the linked documents.
items.cn: 万维网约在 1989 年于欧洲核子研究中心命名，web 很快被用在这些相互链接的文档上。

items.en: Website was formed by joining web and site; the exact first printed use is uncertain.
items.cn: website 由 web 与 site 拼接而成，确切首次印行年代不确定。

items.en: The word replaced older phrases such as web site, and site alone now usually means the same thing.
items.cn: 这个词取代了 web site 等较早写法，如今单说 site 通常也指同一事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers web words that are easily confused with it; the near-meaning group gathers online places and their parts.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与之混淆的 web 类词；近义组收网络场所及其组成部分。

entries.definition: One single page inside a website.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网页」，是网站中的单独一页。

entries.definition: The network of linked documents, or a spider's net.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「万维网、网」，即互链文档构成的网络或蛛网。

entries.definition: The person who runs and updates a site.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网站管理员」。

entries.definition: The ability to see, or something seen; not related.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视力、景象」，与 site 同音但无关。

entries.definition: The short form of website; also any piece of ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网站」（website 的简写），也指任何一块地。

entries.definition: One screen of content within a site.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「页面」，是站点内的一屏内容。

entries.definition: A program on a device, which may replace a website.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「应用」，其功能可以替代网站。

entries.definition: A large site that gathers links and services for users.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门户网站」，集中提供链接与服务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English web and Latin situs, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 web 与拉丁语 situs，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: web is the linking, site is the place: a website is a place made of links.
normal.cn: web 是连接，site 是地点：website 就是用链接搭起的地方。

normal.en: A webpage is one page; a website is all the pages at once.
normal.cn: webpage 是一页，website 是全部页面加在一起。

normal.en: Every website has an address, just as a site has a location.
normal.cn: 每个网站都有地址，正如一块地有位置。

normal.en: Visit a website is the usual verb; you do not 'look' a website.
normal.cn: 常用动词是 visit；不能说 look a website。

normal.en: The short form site is used freely in speech.
normal.cn: 口语中常直接用简写 site。

abstract.en: Picture many rooms joined by corridors with a sign on every door: the corridors are the web, the rooms are the site.
abstract.cn: 想象许多房间由走廊相连，每扇门上挂着招牌：走廊是 web，房间群是 site。

abstract.en: The word joins an old cloth image to a very old idea of a place, and the result is a place without ground.
abstract.cn: 这个词把古老的布料意象接到同样古老的「地点」观念上，结果是一个没有土地的地点。

abstract.en: One address, many pages: the word is singular because the whole is one place.
abstract.cn: 一个地址，许多页面：这个词用单数，因为整体是一处地方。

examples.en: The school website posts the exam timetable every term.
examples.cn: 学校网站每学期都会发布考试时间表。

examples.en: She built her own website to sell the cloth she weaves.
examples.cn: 她自建网站出售自己织的布。

examples.en: Please check the website for the opening hours.
examples.cn: 开放时间请查看网站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网（web）下的赛特（site）」——网上搭起的一座赛特城：网站

root: 由现代英语 web（古英语「织网」，万维网）与 site（拉丁语 situs「位置」，经法语）在二十世纪九十年代拼合而成；相关词有 webpage、webmaster。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of website move from a set of linked pages, to an organisation's online home, to a shop, to one whole domain, and finally to the short spoken form.
sensesIntro.cn: website 的五个义项从相互链接的页面，到机构的网络门面，到网店，到整个域名下的站点，最后是口语简写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rooms joined by corridors, a sign on every door.
core.cn: 核心意象：由走廊相连的房间，每扇门上挂着招牌。

branches.en: LINK LINE: pages joined together under one address.
branches.cn: 链接线：同一地址下彼此的页面相连。

branches.en: HOME LINE: an organisation's public face online.
branches.cn: 门面线：机构在网络上的公开门面。

branches.en: SHOP LINE: a site you can buy from.
branches.cn: 店铺线：可以下单购买的站点。

branches.en: SHORT LINE: speech cuts it to site.
branches.cn: 简写线：口语中缩为 site。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a webpage is one room, a website is the building.
branches.cn: 对照线：webpage 是一个房间，website 是整栋楼。

intro.en: Website is a modern compound whose two halves come from very different places.
intro.cn: website 是现代复合词，其两半来自很不一样的地方。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half has a verifiable Latin origin: situs.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半有可查的拉丁语来源：situs。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 webpage 与 webmaster。

items.example: It forms web-based in related use.

definition_zh: 雄心；抱负；野心；追求的目标；进取心
definition_en: a strong desire to achieve something, especially success, power or a particular aim
core_image: 心里有一团往前推的火，催人不停奔向某个高处
scene: 毕业典礼后的走廊里，两个年轻人靠着窗台谈起将来要做的事。 Her ambition is to run a small clinic in the mountain village where she grew up.
sceneCN: 这里 ambition 是「志向、抱负」（第 1 个义项：想做成某件事的强烈愿望）；句意为她的抱负是在自己长大的山村办一间小诊所。画面里有走廊、窗台与两个谈未来的年轻人。

pos.zh: 名词：雄心；抱负；野心；追求的目标；进取心

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ious 构成，义为「有雄心的；有野心的」
由 ambitious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「雄心勃勃地」
由 ambitious 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「没有抱负的；不图进取的」
由 ambitious 加前缀 over- 构成，义为「野心过大的；目标定得过高的」

senses.title: A strong desire to achieve something
senses.definition: a strong wish to achieve a particular goal, especially one that takes effort and time
senses.definitionCN: 想要达成某个目标的强烈愿望，尤指需要长期努力的目标
senses.example: Her ambition is to run a small clinic in the mountain village where she grew up.
senses.exampleCN: 她的抱负是在自己长大的山村办一间小诊所。
senses.why: Latin ambitio first named the act of going around to gather support; the word then moved from the effort to the desire that drives it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambitio 最初指「四处走动争取支持」这件事，后来从「奔走」转到「驱使人奔走的那股渴望」。

senses.title: A desire for power or status
senses.definition: the desire for power, wealth or high social position, often considered excessive
senses.definitionCN: 对权力、财富或较高社会地位的欲望，常被认为过分
senses.example: His ambition grew with every promotion until he wanted to run the whole company.
senses.exampleCN: 他的野心随着每次升职而膨胀，最后想掌管整个公司。
senses.why: Canvassing for public office was the original scene, so craving office and craving power keep the same word.
senses.whyCN: 奔走拉票本来就是这个词最初的场景，所以「谋求职位」与「渴求权力」一直共用同一个词。

senses.title: A specific aim or objective
senses.definition: the particular thing that a person or group wants to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 某个人或团体想要达成的具体事情
senses.example: Building a village school became a shared ambition of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 建一所村校成了整个山谷共同的志向。
senses.why: The desire attaches itself to a concrete object, and the name of the desire becomes the name of that object.
senses.whyCN: 渴望附着在具体的对象上，于是「渴望」的名字也就成了那个对象的名字。

senses.title: Drive and determination
senses.definition: energy and determination shown in working toward success, without a stated goal
senses.definitionCN: 为取得成功而表现出的精力与决心，未必指向某个明确目标
senses.example: The young coach brought ambition and discipline to a tired team.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻教练给一支疲惫的队伍带来了干劲与纪律。
senses.why: Abstracted from any one aim, the word names the force itself: the push that keeps a person working.
senses.whyCN: 从任何具体目标中抽象出来之后，这个词指的就是那股力本身：推着人持续做事的力量。

senses.title: The aspiration of a group
senses.definition: the collective aim that a company, city or nation sets for itself
senses.definitionCN: 公司、城市或国家为自身设定的集体目标
senses.example: The city's ambition is to become carbon neutral within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的目标是在十年内实现碳中和。
senses.why: A group is treated as a single person with a single desire, so an institution can carry an ambition.
senses.whyCN: 团体被当作一个有单一愿望的个人来看待，所以机构也能「怀抱志向」。

senses.title: The historical sense of canvassing
senses.definition: the older sense of going about among people to seek votes or public office
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的义项：在人群中四处走动以争取选票或公职
senses.example: In Roman elections, ambition meant walking through the city to win support.
senses.exampleCN: 在罗马的选举中，ambition 指的是走遍全城争取支持。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin scene preserved as a historical sense, before the word turned inward into a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语字面场景保留下来的历史义项，那时词义还没有转向内心的感受。

intro.en: Ambition is a Latin political word that travelled through French and slowly turned from an activity into a feeling.
intro.cn: ambition 是一个拉丁语政治词，经法语进入英语，并慢慢从「活动」转成「感受」。

items.en: The verb ambire meant 'to go around', from amb- 'around' and ire 'to go'. In elections it meant to go round the city canvassing for votes.
items.cn: 动词 ambire 意为「绕行」，由 amb-「周围」与 ire「走」构成。在选举语境里指绕城奔走拉票。

items.en: The noun ambitio named 'a going around, a canvassing', and by extension the desire for honour and office that drove it.
items.cn: 名词 ambitio 指「绕行、奔走拉票」，进而指驱使人奔走的求荣与求官之欲。

items.en: The related noun ambitus meant 'a circuit, a compass, an extent', and also carried the political sense of canvassing.
items.cn: 相关名词 ambitus 意为「环绕、范围、周界」，同样带有拉票的政治义。

items.en: Old French ambition took the word into the language of court and office, keeping both the drive and the desire.
items.cn: 古法语 ambition 把这个词带入宫廷与官职的语域，既保留「奔走」也保留「渴望」。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain, since early spellings vary.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入这个名词；由于早期拼写不一，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word splits in tone: aspiration and ambition sound positive, while ambition for power alone sounds negative.
items.cn: 这个词在现代分出声调：抱负与进取听起来是正面的，单纯对权力的野心听起来是负面的。

note.en: The look-alike group is the derived family built on Latin ambire; the near-meaning group gathers aims and drives with different emotional colour.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语 ambire 派生出来的一族词；近义组收各类目标与驱动力，情感色彩不同。

entries.definition: Adjective: having a strong desire to succeed or to achieve something difficult.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有雄心的、有野心的」，指强烈想成功或做成难事。

entries.definition: Adverb: in a manner showing strong desire to succeed.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「雄心勃勃地」，以强烈求成的方式做事。

entries.definition: The scope, extent or limits of something; from Latin ambitus, a going around.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「范围、界限」，来自拉丁语 ambitus「环绕」，与本词同源。

entries.definition: Adjective: lacking ambition or aiming at very little.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「没有抱负的、不图进取的」，由本词族加否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: A hope or ambition of achieving something; more formal and often nobler in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「志向、渴望」，语气更正式，常显得更高尚。

entries.definition: The specific result that a person aims at; concrete and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标」，指具体要达成的结果，中性而不带情感色彩。

entries.definition: Inner energy that pushes a person to work hard; closer to the force than to the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干劲、驱动力」，更接近那股推力而不是目标本身。

entries.definition: Great energy or enthusiasm for a cause; warmer and more emotional than ambition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「热忱、狂热」，对某项事业充满热情，比 ambition 更带情绪温度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin election scene and the family of words it produced.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁选举场景，以及由它产生的一族词展开。

normal.en: amb- is around and ire is to go: ambition began as going around the city.
normal.cn: amb- 是「周围」，ire 是「走」：ambition 最初就是绕城奔走。

normal.en: Canvassing for votes turned into craving office, and craving office turned into craving success.
normal.cn: 拉票变成求官，求官又变成求成功，词义就这样一路内化。

normal.en: Ambitious adds -ious to make the adjective; the noun keeps the bare stem.
normal.cn: ambitious 加 -ious 构成形容词，名词则保留光秃的词干。

normal.en: Ambit keeps the Latin sense of scope, a space marked out around something.
normal.cn: ambit 保留拉丁语的「范围」义，即环绕某物划出的一片空间。

normal.en: Political ambition uses the word in its oldest surviving setting.
normal.cn: political ambition 把这个词用在它最古老的场景里。

abstract.en: Picture a candidate walking a circle around a square, greeting every door: the circle is the ambition and the doors are the votes.
abstract.cn: 想象一位候选人在广场外绕圈，向每一扇门问好：那个圈是 ambition，那些门是选票。

abstract.en: Picture a flame inside a person that leans forward, always toward a higher window.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人心里有一团火，火苗一直向前倾，朝着更高处的窗户。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose top rung is never quite reached; the climbing is the word, not the arrival.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最上面那级总差一点才够到：这个词说的是攀爬，而不是到达。

examples.en: Her ambition is to run a small clinic in the mountain village where she grew up.
examples.cn: 她的抱负是在自己长大的山村办一间小诊所。

examples.en: He had the ambition but not the patience to learn the trade.
examples.cn: 他有雄心，却没有学这门手艺的耐心。

examples.en: The company announced an ambition to cut its waste in half by next year.
examples.cn: 公司宣布了明年把废弃物减半的目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必胜」——心里喊着我一定赢，脚步就停不下来：雄心、野心

root: 拉丁语 ambitio「绕行、奔走拉票」由 ambire「绕行」派生，而 ambire 由 amb-「周围」+ ire「走」构成。字面场景是候选人在城里绕圈争取选票，词义后来从「奔走」转为「求荣求官的渴望」，再泛化为一般的雄心与野心。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses run from the concrete political circuit to the abstract inner flame: the walking, the office sought, the goal named, the drive felt, the aim of a group, and the historical literal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从具体的政治绕行走到抽象的心火：绕城奔走、谋求职位、被命名的目标、被感受到的干劲、团体的志向，以及作为历史义保留下来的字面场景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walks a circle around a crowd, then carries that forward lean inside the chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人绕着人群走一圈，随后把那股前倾的劲头收进胸口。

branches.en: THE ASPIRATION LINE: the desire to achieve something worthy, the modern main sense.
branches.cn: 抱负线：想做成值得之事的那股愿望，是今天的主义。

branches.en: THE POWER LINE: the same desire aimed at office and status, heard as excessive.
branches.cn: 权力线：同一股愿望指向官职与地位，听起来就变得过分。

branches.en: THE OBJECT LINE: the desire hardened into a named aim.
branches.cn: 目标线：愿望凝固成一个有名字的目标。

branches.en: THE FORCE LINE: the desire abstracted into energy and determination.
branches.cn: 力量线：愿望被抽象成精力与决心。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE AND HISTORICAL LINE: a group can have one aim, and the Latin circuit remains as the oldest layer.
branches.cn: 集体与历史线：团体可以共有一个目标，而拉丁语的绕行场景作为最古老的一层保留下来。

intro.en: Ambition is assembled from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb of going, and an abstract noun suffix; the rest of the family grows from the same stem.
intro.cn: ambition 由一个拉丁前缀、一个表示「走」的拉丁动词与抽象名词后缀拼成；词族其余成员也从同一词干生长出来。

latinIntro.en: All the Latin forms here are recorded words, not reconstructions; only the deeper Indo-European layer is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的拉丁语形式都是有文献记录的词，不是重构形式；只有更早的印欧语层次不确定。
