normal.en: The plural is batteries, with -ies.
normal.cn: 复数是 batteries，把 y 变成 ies。

normal.en: Battery life means how long a charge lasts.
normal.cn: battery life 指一次充电能用多久。

normal.en: A flat battery has no power left.
normal.cn: a flat battery 指没电的电池。

normal.en: A battery of tests is a whole set of tests.
normal.cn: a battery of tests 指一整套测试。

normal.en: The word began with guns, not with electricity.
normal.cn: 这个词最早指火炮，与电无关。

abstract.en: See two round cells side by side in a torch.
abstract.cn: 想象手电筒里并排两节圆电池。

abstract.en: See the light dim and die.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光逐渐变暗熄灭。

abstract.en: See a row of guns on a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象山丘上一排火炮。

examples.en: The battery in my torch had gone flat.
examples.cn: 我手电筒里的电池没电了。

examples.en: The doctor ordered a battery of tests.
examples.cn: 医生安排了一组检查。

examples.en: The battery fired at dawn.
examples.cn: 炮兵连在黎明开火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 battery 想成一排并排的电池单元，也可以是一排并排的火炮。

root: 源自拉丁语 battuere「击打」，经古法语 baterie「痛击」进入英语，先指一组火炮，再引申为「一组同类事物」，最后指电池。

sensesIntro.en: One word holds guns, groups and electric cells.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词兼指火炮、成组事物与电池。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two round cells side by side in a torch.
core.cn: 核心意象：手电筒里并排两节圆电池。

branches.en: a spare battery
branches.cn: 备用电池

branches.en: battery life
branches.cn: 电池续航时间

branches.en: a battery of tests
branches.cn: 一组测试

branches.en: a battery of questions
branches.cn: 一连串问题

branches.en: the battery fired
branches.cn: 炮兵连开火

intro.en: Battery takes no living prefix; its endings are grammatical.
intro.cn: battery 不接构词前缀，词尾变化只表示语法。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is battuere, to beat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 battuere，意为「击打」。

items.meaning: a set of guns or cells

definition_en: to keep something within limits, especially by rules
core_image: 用一道栏杆把宽阔的空地围成有限的范围
scene: 为了安全，公园限制游客进入正在施工的区域。 For safety, the park restricts visitors from entering the area under construction.
sceneCN: 这里 restrict 是「限制」（第 1 个义项：用规定限定范围或数量）；句意：为了安全，公园限制游客进入正在施工的区域。

senses.title: Limit an amount or area
senses.definition: to limit something such as size, amount or access
senses.definitionCN: 限制大小、数量或进入范围
senses.example: The rules restrict the number of guests.
senses.exampleCN: 规定限制了客人的数量。
senses.why: The Latin source means to draw tight, so a limit narrows what is allowed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为拉紧，因此限制就是收窄允许的范围。

senses.title: Limit freedom
senses.definition: to control what people are free to do
senses.definitionCN: 控制人们可以自由行动的范围
senses.example: Strict rules restrict what students may wear.
senses.exampleCN: 严格的规定约束了学生的穿着。
senses.why: Freedom drawn tight becomes a narrower space of action.
senses.whyCN: 自由被拉紧后，就变成了更小的行动空间。

senses.title: Keep within a range
senses.definition: to keep something inside a particular range or group
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物保持在特定范围或群体内
senses.example: Please restrict your answer to one page.
senses.exampleCN: 请把答案限定在一页之内。
senses.why: Keeping something inside a range is limiting where it may go.
senses.whyCN: 把事物保持在范围内，就是限定它可以去的地方。

intro.en: Restrict comes from Latin restrictus, the past participle of restringere, to draw tight.
intro.cn: restrict 源自拉丁语 restrictus，即 restringere（拉紧）的过去分词。

items.en: Restringere means to bind back.
items.cn: restringere 意为往回捆住。

items.en: Restrictus means drawn tight.
items.cn: restrictus 意为被拉紧的。

items.en: The participle supplies the English adjective and verb.
items.cn: 该分词提供了英语的形容词与动词。

items.en: Restrict covers rules, space and information.
items.cn: restrict 涵盖规则、空间与信息。

items.en: Restrictions appear in law and daily life.
items.cn: restriction 出现在法律与日常生活中。

note.en: Restrict is close to limit and confine, and shares a root with restrain.
note.cn: restrict 与限定、禁闭相近，并与 restrain 同源。

entries.definition: a limit or rule
entries.definitionCN: 限制

entries.definition: limiting freedom
entries.definitionCN: 限制性的

entries.definition: limited in access
entries.definitionCN: 受限制的

entries.definition: to stop something going beyond a point
entries.definitionCN: 限制

entries.definition: to keep within a space or area
entries.definitionCN: 把……限制在内

entries.definition: to control something harmful
entries.definitionCN: 遏制

normalIntro.en: Restrict shares its tight root with strict: strict rules restrict what we do.
normalIntro.cn: restrict 与 strict 共享「拉紧」的词根：严格的规定限制我们的行为。

normal.en: Restrict access means fewer people may enter.
normal.cn: restrict access 意为更少的人可以进入。

normal.en: Restrict someone to a place means keep them there.
normal.cn: restrict someone to a place 意为把人限制在某处。

normal.en: The rules restrict freedom of movement.
normal.cn: 这些规定限制行动自由。

normal.en: The noun restriction is the limit itself.
normal.cn: 名词 restriction 就是限制本身。

normal.en: Compare restrain: restrain pulls back a force, restrict draws a boundary.
normal.cn: 对比 restrain：restrain 拉住力量，restrict 画出边界。

abstract.en: Picture a wide field narrowed by a fence.
abstract.cn: 想象一片宽阔的田地被人用围栏圈窄。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that opens only for a few people.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只为少数人打开的门。

abstract.en: Think of a page with only one small writing space.
abstract.cn: 想象一页只留出小小一块书写空间。

examples.en: Doctors restrict the use of this drug to adults.
examples.cn: 医生把这种药的使用限定在成人范围内。

examples.en: The city restricts traffic in the old town.
examples.cn: 该市限制老城区的交通。

examples.en: He restricts himself to one cup of coffee a day.
examples.cn: 他限定自己每天只喝一杯咖啡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ strict（严格）」——用严格的规定把范围往回收紧，就是限制；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ stringere（拉紧）→ restrictus（被拉紧的）→ restrict，核心义「把范围收紧、划定边界」。

sensesIntro.en: Restrict first limits an amount or area, then limits freedom, and finally keeps something within a range.
sensesIntro.cn: restrict 先指限制数量或范围，再指约束自由，最后指把事物限定在某个区间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fence turning open ground into a small enclosure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道围栏把开阔的空地围成小小的圈。

branches.en: Amount and access are the first things limited.
branches.cn: 数量与进入权限是最先被限制的对象。

branches.en: Rules also narrow personal freedom.
branches.cn: 规则也缩小个人自由。

branches.en: Something is kept inside a chosen range.
branches.cn: 事物被保持在选定的范围内。

branches.en: Limiting access is a common form of controlling freedom.
branches.cn: 限制进入是控制自由的常见方式。

branches.en: A range of action is a kind of small freedom.
branches.cn: 行动范围就是一种有限的自由。

intro.en: Restrict is built on Latin strictus, drawn tight, with the prefix re-.
intro.cn: restrict 建立在拉丁语 strictus（被拉紧的）之上，并带前缀 re-。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere gives the family its tight core: strict, strain, restrict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere 赋予词族「拉紧」的核心：strict、strain、restrict。

items.example: Strict keeps the same tight idea.
items.exampleCN: strict 保留同样的拉紧含义。
restrictive 描述限制性的规则。

definition_zh: 创新；革新；（新）方法、新事物
definition_en: a new idea, method, or product, or the act of creating such new things
core_image: 旧机器旁边摆出一台从没见过的新装置，围着看的人抄下了图纸
scene: 老厂房里摆着一排用了多年的旧设备，墙角却多了一台新样机。 The engineer called the new design a real innovation, not just a small repair.
sceneCN: 这里 innovation 是「创新、新东西」（第 1 个义项：全新的想法、方法或产品），句意为工程师说这项新设计是真正的创新，而不只是一次小修小补。画面里的物件：旧设备、新样机、图纸。

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「创新的；有新意的」
由拉丁词干构成的后备动词，义为「革新；创新」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「创新者；革新者」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「与创新有关的」

senses.title: A new idea or method
senses.definition: a new idea, method, or device, especially one that changes how something is done
senses.definitionCN: 尤指改变了做事方式的新想法、新方法或新装置
senses.example: The online booking system was a real innovation for the small hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 网上预订系统对这家小旅馆来说是真正的创新。
senses.why: Latin novus means new; in- makes it "into the new", so an innovation is something brought into the world as new.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 novus 意为「新的」；in- 使之成为「进入新奇状态」，所以 innovation 是被带进世界的新东西。

senses.title: The act of bringing in new things
senses.definition: the activity of introducing new ideas or methods into a business, school, or industry
senses.definitionCN: 把新想法或新方法引入企业、学校或行业的行为
senses.example: Innovation is what keeps a small company alive in a crowded market.
senses.exampleCN: 创新是让小公司在拥挤的市场中活下来的东西。
senses.why: The noun also names the doing, not only the thing done: it is the process of stepping into the new.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也指「做的过程」而不只是「做成的东西」：它就是走进新事物的过程。

senses.title: A new product on the market
senses.definition: a product or service that is new to the market and often credited to one company
senses.definitionCN: 市场上新出现、往往归功于某家公司的新产品或新服务
senses.example: Their latest innovation is a battery that charges in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最新的革新产品是一种几分钟就能充满电的电池。
senses.why: From the busy workshop it moved to the shop window: each launch is presented as an innovation.
senses.whyCN: 从忙碌的车间走到了橱窗：每一次新品发布都被称为一项 innovation。

senses.title: A change in long-standing habits
senses.definition: a change in well-established customs or habits, sometimes unwelcome at first
senses.definitionCN: 对由来已久的习惯或风俗所做的改变，起初常不受欢迎
senses.example: Replacing the paper register with an app was an innovation nobody asked for.
senses.exampleCN: 用一个应用取代纸质登记簿，是没人要求过的改变。
senses.why: The oldest examples refer to novelties in religion and law, where a new practice always disturbed someone.
senses.whyCN: 最早的例子指宗教与法律上的新做法，新的做法总会惊动某些人。

intro.en: Innovation is a Latin noun of action built on novus "new"; English took it through French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: innovation 是以拉丁语 novus「新的」为基础的拉丁语行为名词，中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective novus "new" is old Latin and related to the adverb novus-derived nunc "now".
items.cn: 形容词 novus「新的」是古老的拉丁词，与表示「现在」的 nunc 有渊源。

items.en: Novare "to make new" yielded the verb innovare, literally "to make new in".
items.cn: novare「使变新」生出动词 innovare，字面是「使里面变新」。

items.en: The abstract noun innovatio "a renewing" was used in late Latin, chiefly for renewal of laws.
items.cn: 抽象名词 innovatio「更新」见于晚期拉丁语，主要用于法律的更新。

items.en: Old French innovacion carried the word into everyday speech during the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中世纪时古法语 innovacion 把这个词带入日常言语。

items.en: From the sixteenth century it named any new practice; business writing later made it a slogan.
items.cn: 十六世纪起它泛指任何新做法；后来的商业写作又让它成为口号。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for "new"; the near-meaning group holds other words for change and novelty.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「新」这一词根；近义组收其他表示「改变、新事物」的词。

entries.definition: A story; as an adjective, new and unusual, built on Latin novus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「小说」，作形容词义为「新颖的」，都基于拉丁语 novus。

entries.definition: The quality of being new, or a small new object sold for fun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「新奇；新奇小玩意」，词根同是「新」。

entries.definition: To make an old building new again, with the prefix re- "again".
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翻新」，前缀 re- 表「再次」，词根仍是「新」。

entries.definition: Something created for the first time, often a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发明」，指首次创造出的东西，常指装置。

entries.definition: A change that repairs a system rather than creating something new.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改革」，指修补制度而非创造新事物。

entries.definition: A sudden important advance, stronger in tone than innovation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突破」，语气比 innovation 更强，强调突然的重要进展。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin root nov- "new" and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用拉丁词根 nov-「新」以及这个词真实的搭配。

normal.en: nov- is new: innovation is the new thing brought in.
normal.cn: nov- 就是「新」：innovation 就是被带进来的新东西。

normal.en: The same root gives novel, novelty and renovate.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 novel、novelty、renovate。

normal.en: Tech firms live or die by technological innovation.
normal.cn: 科技公司的生死取决于技术创新。

normal.en: An innovation is judged by users, not by its inventor.
normal.cn: 创新由用户评判，而不是由发明者评判。

normal.en: Small innovations often beat one big invention.
normal.cn: 许多小创新往往胜过一件大发明。

abstract.en: Think of a door marked in- that opens into a room called new.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着 in- 的门，通向一个叫「新」的房间。

abstract.en: An innovation is a habit the world has not yet learned.
abstract.cn: 创新是世界尚未学会的一种习惯。

abstract.en: Every innovation starts as someone else's odd idea.
abstract.cn: 每一项创新最初都是别人眼里的怪想法。

examples.en: The factory owes its survival to steady innovation.
examples.cn: 这家工厂靠持续创新才得以存活。

examples.en: Cheap solar panels were the decade's biggest innovation.
examples.cn: 廉价太阳能板是那十年最大的创新。

examples.en: Teachers were asked to share one innovation at the meeting.
examples.cn: 会上要求老师们各分享一项创新做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一脑维新」——一脑子的维新想法，就是创新

root: 拉丁语 novus「新的」→ novare「使变新」→ innovare「使里面变新」→ 晚期拉丁语抽象名词 innovatio「更新」，中世纪经古法语 innovacion 进入英语。nov-「新」也见于 novel、novelty、renovate。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the new thing, the act of making it, the product sold, and the change imposed on old habits.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：新东西本身、制造新东西的行为、售卖的新产品，以及强加于旧习惯的改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something never seen before is brought in and set beside the old.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件从未见过的东西被带进来，摆在旧东西旁边。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: a new method enters the way work is done.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：新方法进入做事的流程。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: innovation also names the ongoing act of bringing new things in.
branches.cn: 过程这条线：innovation 也指持续把新东西带进来的行为。

branches.en: THE SHOP WINDOW: the product itself is displayed as an innovation.
branches.cn: 橱窗这条线：产品本身被展示为一项创新。

branches.en: THE OLD CUSTOM: a change in habit is resisted before it is accepted.
branches.cn: 旧风俗这条线：习惯的改变先被抵制，之后才被接受。

branches.en: THE LINK: the thing and the act share the movement into the new.
branches.cn: 连接线：东西与行为共享「走进新」这一动作。

intro.en: Innovation splits into the Latin prefix in-, the root nov- "new", and the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: innovation 可拆为拉丁前缀 in-、「新」词根 nov- 与名词词尾 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus, novare and innovare are all attested, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus、novare、innovare 均有记载，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

items.example: It marks the movement towards the new state.
items.exampleCN: 它标出朝向新状态的动作。

items.example: The root is visible in novel and renovate.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根见于 novel 与 renovate。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整个词族的根基。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an action.

items.meaning: to renew, bring in new things
items.example: The compound gave the French and English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词给出法语与英语的名词。

items.example: It makes the word an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它使这个词成为抽象名词。

items.example: The verb is back-formed from the noun.

latinEntries.meaning: to renew, bring in new things

core_image: 黑夜里门后伸出的影子，让人立刻后退
scene: 电影里有一只可怕的怪物。 The film has a horrible monster.
sceneCN: 这里 horrible 是「可怕的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：电影里有一只可怕的怪物。

senses.title: Causing fear
senses.definition: causing fear or shock
senses.definitionCN: 引起恐惧或震惊的
senses.example: The film has a horrible monster.
senses.exampleCN: 电影里有一只可怕的怪物。
senses.why: This is the core sense of dread.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示恐惧的核心义项。

senses.title: Very unpleasant
senses.definition: very bad or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 非常糟糕、令人不适的
senses.example: We had horrible weather all week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整周都遇上糟糕的天气。
senses.why: Here the word is about discomfort, not fear.
senses.whyCN: 这里说的是不适，而不是恐惧。

intro.en: Horrible comes from Latin horribilis, causing fear.
intro.cn: horrible 来自拉丁语 horribilis，意为引起恐惧的。

items.en: Horrere meant to bristle with fear.
items.cn: horrere 意为因恐惧而汗毛竖起。

items.en: Horribilis meant causing horror.
items.cn: horribilis 意为引起恐惧的。

items.en: Horrible meant terrible.
items.cn: horrible 意为可怕的。

items.en: Horrible meant causing dread.
items.cn: horrible 意为引起恐惧的。

items.en: It also came to mean very unpleasant.
items.cn: 它也引申为非常糟糕的。

note.en: Horrible is compared with look-alike words and with words for what is very bad.
note.cn: 把 horrible 与形近词以及表示糟糕的词作比较。

entries.definition: a feeling of great fear
entries.definitionCN: 恐怖

entries.definition: in a horrible way
entries.definitionCN: 可怕地

entries.definition: deserving respect
entries.definitionCN: 可敬的

entries.definition: very bad or frightening
entries.definitionCN: 可怕的

entries.definition: extremely bad
entries.definitionCN: 可怕的

entries.definition: very unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 糟糕的

normalIntro.en: Horrible describes what makes us step back, from fear or disgust.
normalIntro.cn: horrible 描述让我们因恐惧或厌恶而后退的东西。

normal.en: The film has a horrible monster.
normal.cn: 电影里有一只可怕的怪物。

normal.en: We had horrible weather all week.
normal.cn: 我们整周都遇上糟糕的天气。

normal.en: There was a horrible smell in the kitchen.
normal.cn: 厨房里有一股难闻的味道。

normal.en: He felt horrible after the long journey.
normal.cn: 长途旅行后他感觉很难受。

normal.en: It was a horrible accident.
normal.cn: 那是一起可怕的事故。

abstract.en: Horrible is the mind taking a step backward.
abstract.cn: 可怕，是心往后退了一步。

abstract.en: Some things are horrible and still must be faced.
abstract.cn: 有些东西很可怕，却仍然必须面对。

abstract.en: A horrible memory can lose its shadow with time.
abstract.cn: 可怕的记忆，会随时间失去阴影。

examples.en: The film has a horrible monster.
examples.cn: 电影里有一只可怕的怪物。

examples.en: We had horrible weather all week.
examples.cn: 我们整周都遇上糟糕的天气。

examples.en: There was a horrible smell in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 厨房里有一股难闻的味道。

dict_mnemonic.text: horrible 是「可怕的」，也可指「糟糕的」；horror 是恐怖，horrify 是使恐惧，horribly 是可怕地。

root: 来自拉丁语 horribilis（引起恐惧的），与 horrere（因恐惧而毛发竖起）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Horrible means causing fear, or simply very unpleasant.
sensesIntro.cn: horrible 表示引起恐惧的，也可只表示非常糟糕的。

core.cn: 让身体本能后退的东西。

branches.en: The film has a horrible monster.
branches.cn: 电影里有一只可怕的怪物。

branches.en: It was a horrible accident.
branches.cn: 那是一起可怕的事故。

branches.en: We had horrible weather all week.
branches.cn: 我们整周都遇上糟糕的天气。

branches.en: Fear and disgust can wear one word.
branches.cn: 恐惧与厌恶可以共用一个词。

branches.en: There was a horrible smell in the kitchen.
branches.cn: 厨房里有一股难闻的味道。

intro.en: Horrible builds horribly, horror, and horrify.
intro.cn: horrible 可构成 horribly，并与 horror、horrify 同族。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin horrere, to bristle with fear.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是拉丁语 horrere，意为因恐惧而毛发竖起。

items.example: The horribleness of the scene shocked them.
items.exampleCN: 场面的可怕让他们震惊。

items.example: The film is full of horrors.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影充满恐怖场面。

latinEntries.example: Horrere is the root of horrible.
latinEntries.exampleCN: horrere 是 horrible 的词根。
horribilis 演变为英语的 horrible。

definition_en: something that happens, especially something important or planned
core_image: 日历上的一个圆圈，把某一天紧紧标了出来
scene: 这场音乐节是城里一年中最大的文化活动。 This music festival is the city's biggest cultural event of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 event 是「活动」（第 2 个义项：有组织、按计划举行的场合）；句意：这场音乐节是城里一年中最大的文化活动。

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: something that happens, especially something important
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事情，尤其是重要的事
senses.example: The discovery was a major event in science.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现是科学界的重大事件。
senses.why: The Latin source means an outcome, so an event is what comes out of a situation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为结果，因此事件就是从某种情况中产生的事。

senses.title: A planned occasion
senses.definition: an organized occasion such as a party or festival
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的场合，如聚会或节日庆典
senses.example: The charity holds a fund-raising event each year.
senses.exampleCN: 该慈善机构每年举办一次筹款活动。
senses.why: An occasion planned in advance is an event on the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 提前计划的场合就是日历上的一件活动。

senses.title: A sports contest
senses.definition: one of the races or competitions in a sports meeting
senses.definitionCN: 运动会中的一项比赛
senses.example: The long jump is her best event.
senses.exampleCN: 跳远是她最擅长的项目。
senses.why: A single contest is one scheduled happening within a larger meeting.
senses.whyCN: 单项比赛是大型运动会中安排的一次具体发生。

intro.en: Event comes from Latin eventus, an outcome, from evenire, to come out.
intro.cn: event 源自拉丁语 eventus（结果），来自 evenire（出来、发生）。

items.en: Evenire means to come out or happen.
items.cn: evenire 意为出来或发生。

items.en: Eventus means an outcome.
items.cn: eventus 意为结果。

items.en: Evenement means something that happens.
items.cn: evenement 意为发生的事。

items.en: Event covers important happenings.
items.cn: event 涵盖重要事件。

items.en: It also names planned occasions and contests.
items.cn: 它也指计划好的活动与比赛。

note.en: Event is close to incident and occasion, and is broader than either.
note.cn: event 与事件、场合相近，但比两者都宽泛。

entries.definition: full of happenings
entries.definitionCN: 多事的

entries.definition: quiet and ordinary
entries.definitionCN: 平淡无事的

entries.definition: a possible happening
entries.definitionCN: 可能发生的事

entries.definition: an unusual or unpleasant event
entries.definitionCN: 事件

entries.definition: a time when something happens
entries.definitionCN: 场合

entries.definition: an event or situation
entries.definitionCN: 事务；事件

normalIntro.en: An event is a date circled on the calendar: something happens there.
normalIntro.cn: event 就是日历上被圈出的日子：那天有事情发生。

normal.en: A major event is important enough to remember.
normal.cn: major event 重要到值得记住。

normal.en: A sporting event draws a crowd.
normal.cn: sporting event 会吸引人群。

normal.en: In the event of rain means if rain happens.
normal.cn: in the event of rain 意为如果下雨。

normal.en: Current events are recent news happenings.
normal.cn: current events 是近期新闻事件。

normal.en: Compare incident: an incident is usually small or unpleasant, an event can be planned.
normal.cn: 对比 incident：incident 通常较小或不愉快，event 可以是计划好的。

abstract.en: Picture one day on a calendar circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上有一天被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Imagine a stage waiting for a crowd to arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台等待人群到来。

abstract.en: Think of a page of news filled with big headlines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页写满大标题的新闻。

examples.en: The wedding was the biggest event of the year.
examples.cn: 婚礼是那一年最大的事件。

examples.en: She helped organize a charity event.
examples.cn: 她帮忙组织了一场慈善活动。

examples.en: The team won three events at the games.
examples.cn: 该队在运动会上赢得了三个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「event」听起来像「一万一」——值得记下的大事；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 e-（出）＋ venire（来）→ evenire（发生）→ eventus（结果）→ event，核心义「从情况中产生、发生的事情」。

sensesIntro.en: Event first names anything that happens, then a planned occasion, and finally one contest in a sports meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: event 先指发生的任何事，再指计划好的场合，最后指运动会中的单项比赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a day circled on a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被圈出的一天。

branches.en: Anything important that happens is an event.
branches.cn: 发生的任何重要事情都是事件。

branches.en: Planned occasions are events on a schedule.
branches.cn: 计划好的场合是日程上的活动。

branches.en: One contest is an event within a meeting.
branches.cn: 单项比赛是运动会中的一项赛事。

branches.en: A planned event becomes a remembered happening.
branches.cn: 计划好的活动会成为被记住的事件。

branches.en: Sports meetings are events made of events.
branches.cn: 运动会是由多项赛事组成的活动。

intro.en: Event comes from Latin evenire, to come out, with the noun ending -tus.
intro.cn: event 源自拉丁语 evenire（出来、发生），带名词词尾 -tus。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire, to come, gives event, prevent and invent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire（来）衍生出 event、prevent 与 invent。

items.exampleCN: eventful 描述忙碌多事的时期。

definition_en: the distance from top to bottom, or the quality of being deep and serious
core_image: 一根绳子被慢慢放下去，过了很久才触到底
scene: 船停在湖心，船夫把系着石头的绳子一点点放下去，直到手突然一松。 The depth of the lake surprised the divers.
sceneCN: 这里 depth 指「深度」（第 1 个义项：从上到下的距离）；句意是湖的深度让潜水员吃惊。

senses.title: Distance downward
senses.definition: the distance from the top to the bottom of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物从顶部到底部的距离
senses.example: The depth of the lake surprised the divers.
senses.exampleCN: 湖的深度让潜水员吃惊。
senses.why: Depth is a distance you cannot see from the surface.
senses.whyCN: 深度是从表面看不见的一段距离。

senses.title: The deepest part
senses.definition: the deepest part of a place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某物最深的部分
senses.example: The fish live in the depths of the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鱼生活在海洋深处。
senses.why: A plural turns the measure into a place.
senses.whyCN: 复数把一种度量变成了一个地方。

senses.title: Seriousness of thought or feeling
senses.definition: the quality of being serious, strong or full of meaning
senses.definitionCN: 严肃、强烈或富有意涵的品质
senses.example: The book has a depth that rewards a second reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书有一种值得再读一遍的深刻。
senses.why: A mind, like water, can be shallow or deep.
senses.whyCN: 人的心思像水，可以浅，也可以深。

intro.en: Depth is Old English deop, deep, with the old suffix -th that also makes length and warmth.
intro.cn: depth 是古英语 deop（深）加上古老的名词词尾 -th，length 与 warmth 也是这么来的。

items.en: Deop meant deep, and the suffix -th turned it into a measure.
items.cn: deop 意为深，词尾 -th 把它变成一种度量。

items.en: Depths came to mean the deepest part of the sea.
items.cn: depths 开始指海洋最深的地方。

items.en: Writers used depth for the richness of a mind or a text.
items.cn: 作家用 depth 形容心思或文章的丰厚。

items.en: Painting and later photography spoke of depth in a picture.
items.cn: 绘画与后来的摄影开始谈画面里的纵深。

items.en: It now measures water, space, feeling and argument alike.
items.cn: 如今它同时衡量水、空间、感情与论证。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deep family, and the meaning group moves from distance to richness of mind.
note.cn: 形近组属于 deep 这一家，近义组则从距离走到心思的丰厚。

entries.definition: going far down from the top
entries.definitionCN: 从顶部向下延伸很远的

entries.definition: to make or become deeper
entries.definitionCN: 使变深或变深

entries.definition: very much, or far down
entries.definitionCN: 非常地，或深深地

entries.definition: the space between two points
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间

entries.definition: deep thought or great knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 深刻的思想或渊博的知识

entries.definition: the strength of a feeling
entries.definitionCN: 某种感情的强度

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a rope paid out over dark water and end with a book that asks to be read twice.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从黑暗水面上一点点放出的绳子开始，落到一本值得读两遍的书。

normal.en: Long becomes length, deep becomes depth: the same old ending.
normal.cn: long 变 length，deep 变 depth，用的是同一个古老词尾。

normal.en: A rope that keeps going is measuring depth.
normal.cn: 一直往下走的绳子，正在量深度。

normal.en: The depths are not a number but a place.
normal.cn: 深处不是一个数字，而是一个地方。

normal.en: A shallow pond and a shallow argument both show their bottom.
normal.cn: 浅塘与浅薄的论证，都让人一眼看到底。

normal.en: Depth of field keeps a photograph from looking flat.
normal.cn: 景深让照片不至于看起来是平的。

abstract.en: Picture a stone sinking until the line goes slack.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头下沉，直到绳子松开。

abstract.en: Picture a diver looking up at a distant surface.
abstract.cn: 想象潜水员抬头看向遥远的水面。

abstract.en: Picture a page that seems to have more behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一页文字，背后似乎还藏着东西。

examples.en: The depth of the lake surprised the divers.
examples.cn: 湖的深度让潜水员吃惊。

examples.en: The fish live in the depths of the ocean.
examples.cn: 这种鱼生活在海洋深处。

examples.en: The book has a depth that rewards a second reading.
examples.cn: 这本书有一种值得再读一遍的深刻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 depth 记成「deep 加 th」：deep 是深，th 是名词尾，像 long 变 length，depth 就是深度。

root: 来自古英语 deop（深）加名词词尾 -th，和 long 变 length 是同一条路。它先表示从上到下的距离，后来指最深的地方，再引申为思想与感情的深刻，也在摄影里表示画面的纵深。

sensesIntro.en: From a rope finding the bottom, to the bottom itself, to a mind with more behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从绳子触到底，到底部本身，再到背后还有东西的心思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope keeps feeding out until a stone touches bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳子一直放，直到石头碰到湖底。

branches.en: The first sense is a distance measured downward.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是向下量出的一段距离。

branches.en: The second sense is the bottom as a place you can enter.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是可以进入的底部空间。

branches.en: The third sense is a mind or a text with room behind it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是背后还有空间的心思或文字。

branches.en: A measurement and a location are only one letter apart.
branches.cn: 一种度量与一个地点，只差一个词尾。

branches.en: The sea and a story can both be sounded.
branches.cn: 海洋与故事，都可以测一测深浅。

intro.en: Depth sits in a small native family built on the Old English word for deep.
intro.cn: depth 位于一个小小本族词家族里，全部围绕古英语的「深」。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here: depth is native English, formed with the old suffix -th.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词基：depth 是本族英语，用古老词尾 -th 构成。

items.example: The depth was over ten metres.
The deepness of the snow slowed us.
items.exampleCN: 积雪之深让我们走得很慢。
他们做了一项深入研究。

items.example: The depthless puddle dried at noon.
items.exampleCN: 那浅浅的水洼中午就干了。

items.meaning: the range that stays in focus
items.example: A small opening increases depth of field.

definition_zh: 观点；视角；透视法；洞察力；远景
definition_en: a particular way of seeing or thinking about something, the art of showing depth on a flat surface, or the ability to judge things in proportion
core_image: 站在一个固定的位置透过窗框看出去：位置一换，看到的东西就重排。
scene: 在农夫眼里，这场旱灾是灾难；在水库管理者眼里，却是喘息之机。 From the perspective of a farmer, the drought is a disaster; from the reservoir's, it is a reprieve.
sceneCN: 这里 perspective 是「看问题的角度」（第 1 个义项：视角、观点）；句意：从农民的角度看，这场干旱是灾难；从水库的角度看，却是喘息之机。场景要点：干裂的田、下降的水位标尺；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观点；视角；透视法；洞察力；远景

collocations.zh: 正确看待某事；把某事放到应有的比例中

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: a particular way of looking at or thinking about something, shaped by where you stand
senses.definitionCN: 由于所处位置而形成的看或思考某事的特定方式
senses.example: The novel tells the same event from three perspectives.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说从三个视角讲述同一件事。
senses.why: Latin perspicere meant 'to look through'. Perspective is the view you get from one position, as if looking through a particular opening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perspicere 意为“看穿、看透”。perspective 就是从某一个位置透过特定开口所得到的视野。

senses.title: The ability to judge proportion
senses.titleCN: 分寸感：知道什么更重要
senses.definition: the ability to see how important things really are in relation to each other
senses.definitionCN: 看出事物之间真实轻重关系的能力
senses.example: Losing one game gave the team a sense of perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉一场比赛反而让球队有了分寸感。
senses.why: Depth in a drawing comes from things being the right size relative to distance. Judging importance is the same skill applied to life.
senses.whyCN: 画面中的纵深，来自物体相对于距离的正确大小。判断重要性，是把同一种本事用在生活上。

senses.title: Art: the geometry of depth
senses.titleCN: 透视法：让平面显出纵深
senses.definition: the technique of representing three-dimensional space and depth on a flat surface
senses.definitionCN: 在平面上表现三维空间与纵深的技法
senses.example: The fresco uses linear perspective to draw the eye down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画用线性透视把视线引向走廊深处。
senses.why: Renaissance painters formalized the idea that parallel lines converge to a vanishing point. Seeing 'through' the canvas is the literal source.
senses.whyCN: 文艺复兴画家把“平行线汇聚于消失点”形式化。透过画布“看进去”，正是这个词的字面来源。

senses.title: A distant view
senses.definition: a view, especially a wide or distant one, seen from a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 从某一地点看到的景色，尤指开阔或辽远的
senses.example: The ridge offers a perspective of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊上能看到整个山谷的远景。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense in English: what is seen from here, extending away from the viewer.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最古老的物理义：从这里看出去、向远处铺开的东西。

senses.title: A considered opinion on a matter
senses.definition: a considered attitude or evaluation of a subject, often one among several
senses.definitionCN: 对某主题经过思考的态度或评价，常为多种之一
senses.example: We need the perspective of someone outside the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要一位行业外人士的看法。
senses.why: The visual metaphor becomes argumentative: a standpoint is a place you stand, and what you see from there is your opinion.
senses.whyCN: 视觉比喻变成论辩性的：立场就是你站的地方，从那里看到的东西就是你的观点。

senses.title: Psychology: taking another's viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 换位思考：站到别人的位置
senses.definition: in psychology, the capacity to understand another person's point of view
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中理解他人视角的能力
senses.example: Perspective-taking improves negotiation outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 换位思考能改善谈判结果。
senses.why: The word is used literally here: you imagine standing where the other stands, and the scene rearranges itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里用的是字面义：你想象站到对方所站的位置，整个场景就重新排列了。

senses.title: Proportion restored: in perspective
senses.titleCN: 比例复原：把事放回它的尺寸
senses.definition: in the phrase in perspective, shown at its true relative size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in perspective，表示按真实的相对大小或重要性来看
senses.example: The loss looks small when seen in perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 从整体比例看，这点损失显得很小。
senses.why: In a correct drawing, near things are large and far things small. Seeing something 'in perspective' is seeing it at the size its distance deserves.
senses.whyCN: 在正确的画里，近的大、远的小。把某事“in perspective”看，就是按它的距离应得的大小去看。

senses.title: Geometry: projection from a viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 投影法：从视点投出去的几何
senses.definition: in geometry, the system that projects a scene onto a plane from a chosen point
senses.definitionCN: 几何中从选定视点把场景投射到平面上的体系
senses.example: Perspective projection distorts parallel lines, unlike orthographic projection.
senses.exampleCN: 与正交投影不同，透视投影会使平行线产生畸变。
senses.why: The artistic technique becomes a mathematical one: a chosen eye point and a plane, with straight lines from one to the other.
senses.whyCN: 艺术技法变成了数学体系：一个选定的眼点、一个平面，以及从一点到另一点的直线。

intro.en: Perspective is Latin perspicere 'to look through' turned into a noun. English first used it for the science of sight, then for the painter's technique, and only later for a mental point of view.
intro.cn: perspective 是拉丁语 perspicere“看穿”名词化的结果。英语先用它指视觉的科学，再指画家的技法，最后才指心里的观点。

items.en: Specere meant 'to look, see'. It is the root behind spectacle, inspect, respect, and perspective.
items.cn: specere 意为“看、看见”。它是 spectacle、inspect、respect、perspective 的词根。

items.en: Perspicere was per- 'through' + specere 'look': 'to see through, look at closely, perceive clearly'.
items.cn: perspicere 是 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”：“看透、仔细看、清楚感知”。

items.en: Perspectiva was the medieval Latin term for the science of optics, literally 'the things of seeing through'.
items.cn: perspectiva 是中古拉丁语对光学的称呼，字面是“看穿的诸事”。

items.en: English takes perspective in the 14th century as the name of the optical science. It is a learned term before it is an everyday one.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 perspective，作为光学学科的名称。它先是学术用语，后才进入日常。

items.en: The artistic sense, the technique of showing depth on a flat surface, is recorded by the 1590s. The scientific name becomes a painter's tool.
items.cn: 艺术义（在平面上表现纵深的技法）于 16 世纪 90 年代见于记录。学科名称变成了画家的工具。

items.en: The sense 'a view from a place' is recorded by the 1660s; the figurative 'mental point of view' by 1762. The metaphor of standing somewhere and looking is fully in place.
items.cn: “从某处看到的景色”义于 17 世纪 60 年代见于记录；比喻性的“心理观点”义于 1762 年。站在某处张望的比喻至此完全成形。

note.en: The first group shares the specere 'look' root; the second collects words for a way of seeing or judging.
note.cn: 第一组共享 specere“看”词根；第二组收“看事物的方式”类词。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things. It comes from the same perspicere but describes a person, not a viewpoint.
entries.definitionCN: 观察敏锐、理解快的。它同出 perspicere，但描述人，而不是视角。

entries.definition: having a ready insight into things; mentally sharp. A formal adjective from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 对事物有敏锐洞察力的；心智锐利的。同出那个拉丁动词的正式形容词。

entries.definition: a possibility of a future event, or a view ahead. Pro- 'forward' + specere 'look'; the direction is forward, not through.
entries.definitionCN: 未来事件的可能性，或前方的景色。pro-“向前”+ specere“看”；方向是向前，不是穿透。

entries.definition: relating to perspective or to a point of view
entries.definitionCN: 与透视或视角有关的（由 perspective 派生）

entries.definition: a person's opinion or way of thinking. It is the everyday equivalent of perspective and lacks the art and depth senses.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的意见或思考方式。它是 perspective 的日常对应词，没有艺术与纵深的义项。

entries.definition: a position from which a subject is considered, often in debate. It keeps the physical 'standing place' image openly.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑某主题时所处的立场，常用于论辩。它明着保留“站立之处”的意象。

entries.definition: a way of approaching a subject, especially one chosen to make it interesting. It is more informal and tactical.
entries.definitionCN: 切入某主题的方式，尤指为使它有趣而选择的。它更口语、更具策略性。

entries.definition: a person's attitude to life, or a forecast. It is broader and often about mood rather than analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对生活的态度，或前景预测。它更宽，常关于情绪而非分析。

entries.definition: a position giving a good view. It is the literal place from which a perspective is obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 能获得良好视野的位置。它就是取得某种 perspective 的字面地点。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin per- 'through' + specere 'look', giving perspicere 'see through'. Family words perspective, perspectival, perspectivism; relatives prospect, inspect, respect, spectacle.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”，合成 perspicere“看透”。词族为 perspective、perspectival、perspectivism；亲属词 prospect、inspect、respect、spectacle。

normal.en: Spectare is 'look': perspective is looking through a particular opening.
normal.cn: spectare 是“看”：perspective 就是透过某个特定开口去看。

normal.en: Prospect looks forward, perspective looks through; same verb, different prefix.
normal.cn: prospect 向前看，perspective 穿透看；同一动词，不同前缀。

normal.en: Linear perspective was a Renaissance rule: parallels meet at a vanishing point.
normal.cn: 线性透视是文艺复兴的规则：平行线在消失点相交。

normal.en: In perspective means at the size the distance deserves.
normal.cn: in perspective 就是按距离应得的大小来看。

normal.en: Perspective-taking is imagination used as a measuring instrument.
normal.cn: 换位思考，是把想象力当量尺来用。

abstract.en: Perspective is not a better view; it is a different place to stand.
abstract.cn: 视角不是更好的视野，而是另一个站立之处。

abstract.en: Depth exists only because some things are allowed to be small.
abstract.cn: 纵深之所以存在，只因有些东西被允许变小。

abstract.en: The ability to change perspective is the cheapest form of mercy.
abstract.cn: 能换一个视角，是最廉价的慈悲。

examples.en: Try to see the decision from the perspective of a new employee.
examples.cn: 试着从新员工的角度看这个决定。

examples.en: The bad quarter should be put into perspective against ten years of growth.
examples.cn: 这个糟糕的季度应当放到十年增长的比例中来看。

examples.en: Brunelleschi's experiment demonstrated linear perspective in painting.
examples.cn: 布鲁内莱斯基的实验展示了绘画中的线性透视。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破视野·派克提夫”——派克提着窗框站定，换个位置就换一片视野 → perspective 视角、透视

root: 源自拉丁语 perspicere“看穿、看清”，由 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”构成；中世纪拉丁语 perspectiva 是“光学”，英语 14 世纪借入，16 世纪 90 年代转指绘画透视，1660 年代有“景色”义，1762 年才有比喻性的“观点”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of perspective, all one geometry: a viewpoint, a plane, and the lines that connect them.
sensesIntro.cn: perspective 的八个义项是同一个几何关系：一个视点、一个平面，以及连接二者的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye at a fixed point looking through a frame at a scene that recedes to a vanishing point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只眼固定在一点，透过窗框看出去，景物向消失点退去。

branches.en: MIND: where you stand and what you conclude — the viewpoint and the opinion it produces.
branches.cn: 心智：站在哪里与得出什么——视角以及由它产生的看法。

branches.en: EMPATHY: moving your own eye to another point, the viewpoint taken as an act.
branches.cn: 共情：把自己的眼移到另一点，视角由“位置”变成“动作”。

branches.en: PROPORTION: judging importance is drawing depth, and in perspective restores true size.
branches.cn: 比例：判断重要性就是画纵深，而 in perspective 是恢复真实大小。

branches.en: TECHNIQUE: the painter's vanishing point and the geometer's projection are one system, formalized.
branches.cn: 技法：画家的消失点与几何学家的投影，是同一个体系的形式化。

branches.en: LANDSCAPE: the oldest physical sense, what lies spread out in front of the eye.
branches.cn: 景物：最古老的物理义，铺展在眼前的那一片。

intro.en: Perspective's family is built on Latin specere 'to look'. Suffixes mark the adjective and the doctrine; compounds name the techniques and the mental acts.
intro.cn: perspective 的词族建立在拉丁语 specere“看”上。后缀标记形容词与学说；复合词则命名技法与心理活动。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are specere 'look', perspicere 'see through', and perspectiva, the medieval Latin name for optics.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是 specere“看”、perspicere“看透”与 perspectiva——中世纪拉丁语对光学的称呼。

items.meaning: a viewpoint, or the art of showing depth
items.meaningCN: 视角；表现纵深的技法（来自拉丁语 perspectiva）
items.example: The two reports offer opposite perspectives.
items.exampleCN: 两份报告提供了相反的视角。

items.meaning: relating to a perspective or viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 与透视或视角有关的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The drawing has a strong perspectival structure.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画有很强的透视结构。

items.meaning: the view that knowledge is always from some perspective
items.meaningCN: 认为知识总是出自某种视角的主张（-ism 构成主义名词）
items.example: Nietzsche's perspectivism denies a view from nowhere.
items.exampleCN: 尼采的视角主义否认存在“无处之见”。

items.meaning: the act of imagining another person's viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 想象他人视角的行为（心理学用语）
items.exampleCN: 换位思考能减少团队冲突。

items.meaning: depth shown by lines converging on a vanishing point
items.meaningCN: 用线条汇聚于消失点来表现纵深（艺术术语）
items.example: The street is drawn in strict linear perspective.
items.exampleCN: 这条街用严格的线性透视画出。

items.meaning: depth shown by making distant things hazier and bluer
items.meaningCN: 通过使远处景物更朦胧、更偏蓝来表现纵深
items.example: The mountains fade by aerial perspective.
items.exampleCN: 群山因空气透视而渐淡。

items.meaning: seen at its true relative size or importance
items.meaningCN: 按真实的相对大小或重要性来看
items.example: The problem looks manageable in perspective.
items.exampleCN: 放到整体里看，问题并不难办。

items.meaning: to compare something so that its real importance becomes clear
items.meaningCN: 通过比较使某事的真实重要性显现
items.example: The figures put the loss into perspective.
items.exampleCN: 这些数字让损失的大小变得清楚。

items.meaning: a projection from a viewpoint that makes far things smaller
items.meaningCN: 从视点投射、使远处物体变小的投影法
items.example: Games use perspective projection to create depth.
items.exampleCN: 游戏用透视投影制造纵深。

items.meaning: a drawing made according to the rules of depth
items.example: The class began with perspective drawing.

definition_en: far below a surface, or to a very great degree
core_image: 一颗石子沉进水里，一直落到看不见的深处
scene: 她把话说得很慢，眼睛看着桌角，像是从很里面取出来的。 She was deeply moved by the letter.
sceneCN: 这里 deeply 指「深深地」（第 1 个义项：一直落到内部很深处）；句意是那封信让她深受触动。

senses.title: Far below the surface
senses.definition: at or towards a great distance below a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面以下很深的地方
senses.example: The anchor sank deeply into the soft mud.
senses.exampleCN: 锚深深地陷进软泥里。
senses.why: Depth is measured by how far a thing travels downward.
senses.whyCN: 深度就是看一样东西往下走了多远。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: very much, used with feelings, needs and beliefs
senses.definitionCN: 非常，多与情感、需要和信念连用
senses.example: She was deeply moved by the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让她深受触动。
senses.why: A feeling that reaches the bottom of us cannot be called mild.
senses.whyCN: 一直落到心底的感受，就不能算轻微。

senses.title: In a thorough and serious way
senses.definition: in a careful and thorough manner, of thought or study
senses.definitionCN: 在思考或研究上认真而透彻
senses.example: He thought deeply before he gave his answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他深思之后才给出回答。
senses.why: Thinking that goes far down is thinking done well.
senses.whyCN: 想得够深，才算想得够好。

intro.en: Deeply is deep plus the old adverb ending -ly, and deep goes back to an Old English word for a low place.
intro.cn: deeply 是 deep 加古老的副词词尾 -ly；deep 则来自古英语中表示低处的词。

items.en: Deop named the sea and any hollow place that went far down.
items.cn: deop 指大海，也指任何往下很深的凹陷之处。

items.en: The adverb ending -lice was already shortening to -ly.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -lice 当时已经在缩成 -ly。

items.en: Writers used deeply for both sunken things and strong feelings.
items.cn: 作家用它同时写沉下去的东西和强烈的感情。

items.en: Deeply settled into phrases about grief, sleep and debt.
items.cn: 它稳稳进入描写悲伤、睡眠与债务的说法里。

items.en: Today it mostly measures the strength of a feeling or belief.
items.cn: 如今它多半用来衡量情感或信念的强度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deep root, and the meaning group offers stronger adverbs for the same feeling.
note.cn: 形近组共用同一个「深」的根，近义组则给出表示同一种感受的更强副词。

entries.definition: going a long way down from the top
entries.definitionCN: 从上往下延伸很远的

entries.definition: the distance from the top to the bottom
entries.definitionCN: 从上到下的距离

entries.definition: to make or become deeper
entries.definitionCN: 使变深或变得更深

entries.definition: in a way that touches the very bottom of feeling
entries.definitionCN: 以触及情感最深处的方式

entries.definition: with very strong force or feeling
entries.definitionCN: 带着极强的力量或情感

entries.definition: very much, often of respect or thanks
entries.definitionCN: 非常，常用于敬意或感谢

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a stone dropping into still water and end with a thought that goes all the way down.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一颗石子落进静水开始，落到一直想到底的心思。

normal.en: A stone is not loud when it lands; the quiet is how you know it went far.
normal.cn: 石子落水并不响，安静才说明它落得够深。

normal.en: Deep sleep and deep sorrow both take you where no one can follow.
normal.cn: 沉睡与深悲都会把你带到别人跟不进去的地方。

normal.en: When a letter makes your eyes hot, you have been moved deeply.
normal.cn: 一封信让眼睛发热，就是被深深打动了。

normal.en: Roots are never seen; that is why they hold the tree so well.
normal.cn: 根从来看不见，所以才把树抱得那么牢。

normal.en: Add -ly to deep and the depth turns into a manner of doing.
normal.cn: deep 后面加 -ly，深度就变成了一种做事的方式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into dark water and not finding the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进暗水里，怎么也摸不到底。

abstract.en: Picture a word spoken so low that the room leans in to hear it.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话说得极轻，整间屋子都凑过去听。

abstract.en: Picture roots under grass, wider than the branches above.
abstract.cn: 想象草下的根系，比上面的枝叶还要铺得开。

examples.en: We are deeply grateful for all the help you gave us.
examples.cn: 我们非常感激你给予的全部帮助。

examples.en: The well is deeply cut into the hard rock.
examples.cn: 这口井深深地凿进坚硬的岩石里。

examples.en: She breathed deeply and began to speak.
examples.cn: 她深深吸了一口气，开始讲话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deeply 记成「底里」：deep 是深，ly 是「地」，一直到底里，就是深深地。

root: deep 源自古英语 deop，本义是「往下的深处」，可指海，也可指任何凹陷。加副词词尾 -ly 之后，deeply 同时继承了具体与抽象两层意思：既指沉在下面，也指情感、信念或思考达到最深处。

sensesIntro.en: From a stone going down, to a heart that is touched, to a mind that thinks it through.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一颗石子往下沉，到一颗心被打动，再到一个念头被想透。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone sinking until the bottom cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子沉下去，直到看不见底。

branches.en: The first sense is simple distance downward, measured in space.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是往下的距离，用空间来量。

branches.en: The same downward movement, felt in the chest, becomes strong emotion.
branches.cn: 同样的往下，落到胸口，就成了强烈的情感。

branches.en: Applied to thought, depth means care taken to the end.
branches.cn: 用在思考上，深度就是一直做到最后的认真。

branches.en: Space and feeling share one word because both have a bottom.
branches.cn: 空间与情感共用一个词，因为两者都有底。

branches.en: A strong feeling and a deep thought are both things we do not skim.
branches.cn: 强烈的感受与深刻的思考，都是不能草草掠过的东西。

intro.en: Deeply belongs to the deep family: a verb of deepening, a noun of depth and a set of compounds.
intro.cn: deeply 属于 deep 这一族：有表示加深的动词、表示深度的名词，还有一批复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in deeply; both parts are native English.
latinIntro.cn: deeply 里没有拉丁成分，两个部分都是英语本族语。

items.meaning: in a deep or intense way
items.example: They talked deeply into the night.
The lake is deep in the middle.
The river deepens after the bend.
items.exampleCN: 河流转过弯之后变深了。

items.meaning: the measure of how deep something is
items.example: They measured the depth of the pool.
The deepness of his voice filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 他低沉的嗓音充满大厅。

items.meaning: firmly fixed and hard to change
items.exampleCN: 这是一个根深蒂固的习惯。

items.meaning: long established and hard to remove
items.example: The fear was deep-rooted in the village.
items.exampleCN: 这种恐惧在村里根深蒂固。

items.meaning: found in the far part of the sea

definition_zh: 否定的；负面的；消极的；负的；负数；底片
definition_en: saying no or refusing; harmful or unwelcome; less than zero; and, as a noun, a number below zero, a film image with light and dark reversed, or a denying word
core_image: 一个减号落在数字前面，把整条刻度推向另一边
scene: 实验记录摊在桌上，最后一列数字前面都带着减号，组长让大家重新核对每一根接线。 The meter gave a negative reading, so the team checked every connection again.
sceneCN: 这里「negative」是「负的、负数的」（第 3 个义项：小于零的数值）；句意是仪表给出负值，于是全组把每处接线重新查了一遍。图中可辨识物件：实验记录、减号、仪表、接线。

derivatives.zh: 由 negative 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「否定地；负面地」
由 negative 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「消极性；负面情绪」
由拉丁 negare 进入英语，义为「否定；取消」

senses.title: Saying no or refusing
senses.definition: expressing refusal or denial, rather than agreement
senses.definitionCN: 表示拒绝或否认，而不是同意
senses.example: She gave a negative answer without looking up.
senses.exampleCN: 她头也没抬，给了一个否定的回答。
senses.why: Latin negare meant to say no, and the adjective negativus simply carried that refusal into a describing word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 negare 意为说「不」，形容词 negativus 只是把这份拒绝带进描述性的词里。

senses.title: Harmful, unwelcome or pessimistic
senses.definition: having a bad or harmful effect, or showing a lack of hope and confidence
senses.definitionCN: 带来不良或有害影响，或表现出缺少希望与信心
senses.example: The new rules had a negative effect on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定对小店铺产生了负面影响。
senses.why: A refusal pushes something away, and what is pushed away is often felt as harm; from 'saying no' the word slides to 'working against you'.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝就是把某物推开，而被推开的东西往往让人觉得有害；于是词义从「说不」滑向「对你不利」。

senses.title: Less than zero
senses.definition: below zero on a scale, or represented with a minus sign
senses.definitionCN: 刻度上小于零，或用减号表示
senses.example: Minus five is a negative number.
senses.exampleCN: 负五是一个负数。
senses.why: A minus sign reverses direction on a number line, so the word for denial also marks values that fall on the other side of zero.
senses.whyCN: 减号在数轴上把方向反过来，所以表示否认的词也用来标记落在零另一边的数值。

senses.title: A film image with light and dark reversed
senses.definition: a piece of film or paper on which light and dark, and often colours, are reversed
senses.definitionCN: 明暗乃至颜色被反转的胶片或相纸
senses.example: He kept the old negatives in a paper envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧底片收在一个纸信封里。
senses.why: In a photographic negative the picture is turned inside out, bright sky becoming dark; the word names that reversal, which is its oldest visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 在照相底片上，画面是反过来的，明亮的天空变成暗色；这个词命名的正是这种反转，也是它最古老的视觉义。

intro.en: Negative comes from a Latin verb for saying no, and the idea of reversal runs through denial, harm, below-zero values and film.
intro.cn: negative 出自拉丁语中表示说「不」的动词，「反转」这个观念贯穿否认、损害、零下数值与胶片。

items.en: A reconstructed negative particle lies far behind the Latin family for denying, though its exact form is not certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语这一族表示否认的词，远处可追到一个重构的否定小词，但其确切形式并不确定。

items.en: negare meant to say no, to refuse or deny; how its internal parts were formed is still debated.
items.cn: negare 意为说「不」、拒绝或否认；它内部如何构成至今仍有争论。

items.en: negativus was the adjective for denying or refusing, built on the stem with the ending -ivus.
items.cn: negativus 是表示否认或拒绝的形容词，由词干加 -ivus 构成。

items.en: Middle English took negatif from French and used it first for a statement that denies something.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语借来 negatif，最早用来指否定某事的陈述。

items.en: Modern English widens negative to harmful effects, numbers below zero and the reversed image on film.
items.cn: 现代英语把 negative 扩展到有害影响、零以下数值，以及胶片上反转的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of denial and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers words for harm, refusal and their opposites.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语表示否认的动词及其词尾展开；近义组收表示损害、拒绝以及相反概念的词。

entries.definition: To deny something or make it ineffective.
entries.definitionCN: 否定某事或使其失效。

entries.definition: The act of denying, or a statement that denies.
entries.definitionCN: 否认的行为，或表示否认的陈述。

entries.definition: The quality of being negative, or a gloomy attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 消极性；阴沉的态度。

entries.definition: In a negative manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以否定或消极的方式。

entries.definition: Expressing agreement, or showing hope and confidence.
entries.definitionCN: 表示同意，或表现出希望与信心。

entries.definition: Unfavourable and likely to cause harm.
entries.definitionCN: 不利的，容易造成损害的。

entries.definition: Expecting bad outcomes rather than good ones.

normalIntro.en: The word begins with a Latin no and ends by marking anything turned the other way: a reply, an effect, a number, a photograph.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语的「不」出发，最后用来标记一切被翻到另一面的东西：回答、影响、数字、照片。

normal.en: Negare is the Latin verb 'to deny', and negativus is its adjective, so the family is regular once the verb is known.
normal.cn: negare 是拉丁语「否认」动词，negativus 是它的形容词；记住动词，这一族词就顺了。

normal.en: The prefix neg- carries the sense of no, the same element heard in negate and negation.
normal.cn: neg- 这个成分带着「不」的意思，在 negate 与 negation 里也能听到。

normal.en: Negative feedback does not mean bad feedback; it means feedback that pushes back against the current state.
normal.cn: negative feedback 不是「坏反馈」，而是往回压、抵消当前状态的那种反馈。

normal.en: In the negative is a formal way of saying that the answer is no.
normal.cn: in the negative 是「回答是否定的」的正式说法。

normal.en: A photographic negative reverses light and dark, which makes the word's idea of reversal visible.
normal.cn: 照相底片把明暗反过来，让这个词的「反转」观念看得见。

abstract.en: A minus sign is a small mark that flips the whole direction of a number, much like a single no can flip a decision.
abstract.cn: 一个减号就能把数字的方向整个翻过来，很像一句「不」能翻掉一个决定。

abstract.en: Calling an effect negative is a way of saying it pushes against what we wanted.
abstract.cn: 把某种影响叫作负面，等于说它顶着我们想要的方向推。

abstract.en: The film negative stores a picture by keeping the opposite of every light and shadow.
abstract.cn: 底片靠保存每处明暗的相反值来存下一幅画面。

examples.en: She gave a negative answer without looking up.
examples.cn: 她头也没抬，给了一个否定的回答。

examples.en: The new rules had a negative effect on small shops.
examples.cn: 新规定对小店铺产生了负面影响。

examples.en: Minus five is a negative number.
examples.cn: 负五是一个负数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捏个提物」——捏着鼻子提不起劲，看什么都往坏处想；记住 negative 是否定的、负面的。

root: 拉丁语 negare（否认）加形容词后缀 -ivus 构成 negativus；negare 的更早来源一般认为与否定小词有关，但具体构成仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a no that turns things the other way; the senses divide into refusal, harm, values below zero and the reversed photographic image.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一句把事物翻到另一面的「不」；义项分出拒绝、损害、零以下数值，以及反转的照相影像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a minus sign landing in front of a figure and pushing the whole scale the other way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个减号落在数字前面，把整条刻度推向另一边。

branches.cn: 话还没出口，头先摇了一下

branches.cn: 新规之后小店客人变少

branches.cn: 温度计落到零刻度以下

branches.en: a paper envelope holding reversed pictures
branches.cn: 纸信封里装着明暗反转的影像

branches.en: a form with the no box ticked
branches.cn: 表格上「否」的那一格被勾中

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the root of denial, its verb negare and the derived adjective negativus; the English endings then build the modern forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示否认的词根、动词 negare 与派生形容词 negativus，英语词尾再搭出现代形式。

definition_en: a standard by which something is judged or decided
core_image: 评委桌上摊着一张打分表，一条条标准逐项勾选
scene: 评委把打分表铺在桌上，一行行对照。 Cost was not the only criterion for the choice.
sceneCN: 这里 criterion 指「标准」（第 1 个义项：用来评判或决定事物的依据）；句意是成本并不是这次选择的唯一标准。

senses.title: A standard for judging
senses.definition: a standard by which something is judged or decided
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判或决定某事物的标准
senses.example: Safety is our first criterion.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是我们的第一标准。
senses.why: To choose one thing you must first know what counts.
senses.whyCN: 要挑出一样东西，先得知道什么才算数。

senses.title: One test in a set
senses.definition: one of several tests used together to compare choices
senses.definitionCN: 几项测试之一，共同用来比较各种选择
senses.example: The committee listed five criteria for the award.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为这个奖项列了五项评判指标。
senses.why: A single test can be fooled; several together rarely are.
senses.whyCN: 单独一项测试容易被骗，几项一起就很难。

senses.title: A rule for sorting
senses.definition: a rule used to put things into groups
senses.definitionCN: 用来把事物分进各组的规则
senses.example: Size is a useful criterion for sorting the samples.
senses.exampleCN: 大小是给样本分类的一个有用依据。
senses.why: To sort is to decide, and every decision needs a rule.
senses.whyCN: 分类就是做决定，而每个决定都需要一条规则。

intro.en: Criterion comes from Greek kriterion, a means of judging, from krites, a judge.
intro.cn: criterion 源自希腊语 kriterion（判断的手段），再往上是 krites（法官）。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate, to decide or to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开、决定或判断。

items.en: Krites named a judge or an interpreter.
items.cn: krites 指法官或解释者。

items.en: Kriterion named the tool or test used to judge.
items.cn: kriterion 指用来判断的工具或检验。

items.en: Criterion entered English as a word for a test of truth.
items.cn: criterion 作为检验真伪的词进入英语。

items.en: It spread to science, business and daily choices.
items.cn: 它扩展到科学、商业与日常选择。

items.en: Its Greek plural criteria is now more common than criterions.
items.cn: 它的希腊式复数 criteria 现在比 criterions 更常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crit- stem, and the meaning group names other standards of judgement.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crit- 词干，近义组列出其他用于评判的标准。

entries.definition: a person who judges works
entries.definitionCN: 评判作品的人

entries.definition: very important or very serious
entries.definitionCN: 非常重要的或非常严重的

entries.definition: the plural form of criterion

entries.definition: a level of quality people expect

entries.definition: a way of judging size or worth

entries.definition: a known point used for comparison

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a score sheet and end with a rule for sorting boxes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一张评分表开始，最后落到分箱子的规则。

normal.en: Criterion and critic share a root: the judge and the ruler.
normal.cn: criterion 与 critic 同根：一个是尺，一个是拿尺的人。

normal.en: A criterion is a ruler you cannot see.
normal.cn: 标准是一把看不见的尺。

normal.en: Five boxes ticked, one choice made.
normal.cn: 五个格子打完勾，一个选择就定了。

normal.en: No criterion means no argument, only taste.
normal.cn: 没有标准，就没有争论，只剩口味。

normal.en: Criteria is one word wearing a Greek plural.
normal.cn: criteria 是一个披着希腊复数的词。

abstract.en: Picture a clean sheet with neat rows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干净的表，横线排得整齐。

abstract.en: Picture a hand hovering over two boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在两个格子之间悬着。

abstract.en: Picture two piles sorted by one line.
abstract.cn: 想象两堆东西按同一条线分开。

examples.en: Price is only one criterion for buying a car.
examples.cn: 价格只是买车的一项标准。

examples.en: The plan failed to meet the safety criteria.
examples.cn: 这项计划未能符合安全标准。

examples.en: Kindness was her main criterion for a friend.

root: 源自希腊语 kriterion（判断的手段），再往上是 krinein（分开、判断）；本义是「用来判定真假好坏的那把尺」，即标准与准则。

sensesIntro.en: From one standard of judgement, to a set of tests, to a rule for sorting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一条评判标准，到一组检验指标，再到一条分类规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a score sheet with neat rows of ticks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张横线整齐、逐项打勾的评分表。

branches.en: A standard tells us what counts as good.
branches.cn: 标准告诉我们什么才算好。

branches.en: Several tests together guard against one false signal.
branches.cn: 几项检验合起来，防止一个假信号。

branches.en: A rule of sorting turns a crowd into groups.
branches.cn: 一条分类规则把一堆东西分成几组。

branches.en: Each test borrows its authority from the same standard.
branches.cn: 每项检验的权威都来自同一条标准。

branches.en: Testing and sorting are both acts of separating.
branches.cn: 检验和分类，都是把东西分开的动作。

scene: 报告里列了三处小错，但没有改变结论。 The report listed three minor errors, none of which changed the conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 minor 是「轻微的、不严重的」（第 3 个义项：程度轻、不严重）；句意：报告列出三处轻微错误，没有一处改变结论。场景要点：一份校样上三处小小的红笔改动、旁边依然通过的结论页、天平上微微上翘的一端；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The smaller of two things
senses.definition: smaller in size, extent, or number when compared with a paired thing
senses.definitionCN: 与配对的事物相比，在尺寸、范围或数量上更小
senses.example: The minor axis of the ellipse is the shorter one.
senses.exampleCN: 椭圆的短轴就是较短的那条轴。
senses.why: Latin minor is a comparative, 'smaller'. It does not mean small in general but smaller than the other member of a pair, which is why the word so often appears beside major.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minor 是比较级，意为“更小的”。它不是泛泛地表示小，而是比同一对里的另一个更小，因此这个词常与 major 并出现。

senses.title: Less important: a secondary part
senses.definition: less important, powerful, or influential than the main person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 不如主要的人或事物重要、有力量或有影响
senses.example: He played a minor role in the negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 他在谈判中只起了次要作用。
senses.why: Rank is treated as weight on a balance. The lighter pan rises, and whatever sits there is minor: present, but not carrying the decision.
senses.whyCN: 等级被当成天平上的重量。较轻的那一端会翘起，放在那一端的东西就是 minor：它在场，却不承担决定。

senses.title: Slight: not serious
senses.definition: small enough in degree to be unimportant or easy to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 程度小到无关紧要或容易处理
senses.example: She suffered only minor injuries in the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 她在撞车中只受了轻伤。
senses.why: The comparison has faded and only the smallness remains. A minor injury is not measured against a major one; it is simply below the threshold of seriousness.
senses.whyCN: 比较对象已经淡去，只剩下“小”。轻伤并不是拿来与重伤对比，它只是落在“严重”这道门槛之下。

senses.title: Underage: below the legal age
senses.titleCN: 未成年的：低于法定年龄
senses.definition: not yet old enough to have full legal rights or responsibilities
senses.definitionCN: 年龄尚不足以拥有完整法律权利或承担责任
senses.example: Minor children must be accompanied by an adult.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年子女必须由成年人陪同。
senses.why: Age is another scale, and the legal threshold is the line between full and lesser status. A person below that line is minor in the eyes of the law.
senses.whyCN: 年龄是另一把尺子，法定门槛就是完整身份与次一等身份之间的界线。线以下的人在法律眼里就是 minor。

senses.title: Music: a minor key or interval
senses.definition: in music, belonging to a key or interval built on a minor third, shorter than the corresponding major one
senses.definitionCN: 在音乐中，属于以小三度构成的小调或音程，比对应的大调或大音程更短
senses.example: The second movement slips into a minor key.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章转入了小调。
senses.why: The interval is literally lesser: a minor third is shorter than the major third. The word keeps its comparative sense inside music theory.
senses.whyCN: 这个音程字面上就是“较小的”：小三度比大三度短。这个词在乐理内部保留了它的比较级含义。

senses.title: Sports: the minor leagues
senses.definition: in sport, the leagues or competitions below the top professional level
senses.definitionCN: 体育中低于顶级职业水平的联赛或赛事
senses.example: He spent four seasons in the minor leagues before being called up.
senses.exampleCN: 他在小联盟打了四个赛季才被上调。
senses.why: The league table is a ranking, and the minor leagues sit one step below the major ones. The word marks position on that ladder, not the size of the players.
senses.whyCN: 联赛表就是一张排名，小联盟坐在大联盟下面一级。这个词标记的是梯子上的位置，而不是球员的体型。

senses.title: Logic: the minor premise
senses.definition: in a syllogism, the premise that contains the subject of the conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 在三段论中，包含结论主项的那个前提
senses.example: The minor premise says that Socrates is a man.
senses.exampleCN: 小前提说苏格拉底是人。
senses.why: A syllogism has a greater and a lesser premise. The one carrying the subject is the lesser member of the pair, so it inherited the name minor.
senses.whyCN: 三段论有一个大前提和一个小前提。承载主项的那一个是这对命题中较小的一员，于是继承了 minor 这个名字。

senses.title: Academic: a secondary subject
senses.definition: a subject studied at university in addition to the main subject, with fewer credits
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里除主修之外学习的科目，所需学分较少
senses.example: She chose history as her minor.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择了历史作为辅修。
senses.why: The degree has a major and a minor: the second subject carries less weight in the total. It is the academic version of the lighter pan.
senses.whyCN: 学位有一个主修和一个辅修：第二门科目在总量里分量更轻。它就是天平上较轻那一端的学业版本。

senses.title: A person below legal age
senses.definition: a person who has not reached the age at which the law grants full adult rights
senses.definitionCN: 尚未达到法律授予完整成年人权利的年龄的人
senses.example: The club is not allowed to sell alcohol to minors.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部不得向未成年人售酒。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by leaving out the person: 'a minor person' shortened to 'a minor'. Legal writing uses it as a stable category.
senses.whyCN: 形容词省略了所修饰的人，变成了名词：“一个未成年的人”缩成“一个未成年人”。法律文本把它用作固定类别。

intro.en: Minor is a Latin comparative borrowed whole, first through the Franciscans and then in general use. Its relation to parvus is grammatical rather than root-based, and that point is disputed in the sources.
intro.cn: minor 是整体借入的拉丁语比较级，先经方济各会进入英语，再进入一般用法。它与 parvus 的关系是语法性的而非词根性的，这一点在资料中存在争议。

items.en: First recorded in English in frere menour 'Franciscan friar', literally 'minor friar', from Latin minor. The order's founder chose Fratres Minores, 'lesser brethren', for humility.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 13 世纪早期，出现在 frere menour“方济各会修士”中，字面是“较小的修士”，来自拉丁语 minor。该会创始人选用 Fratres Minores“小兄弟会”，是出于谦卑。

items.en: Latin minor meant 'less, lesser, smaller, junior', figuratively 'inferior, less important'. It was formed as the masculine/feminine of minus on the mistaken assumption that minus was a neuter comparative. Latin grammars traditionally pair parvus 'small' with minor and minimus, but the roots differ: minor belongs to *mei-, while parvus has a separate origin, itself not fully settled. The pairing is suppletive, grammatical rather than etymological, and its root relation is disputed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 minor 意为“更少、更小、更年幼”，引申为“较低、较不重要”。它是把 minus 误当作中性比较级之后，按阳性／阴性形式造出来的。拉丁语法传统把 parvus“小”与 minor、minimus 配成一组比较级和最高级，但两者词根不同：minor 属于 *mei-，parvus 另有来源，其自身来源也未完全定论。这种配对是异根补充式，属于语法配对而非词源配对，其词根关联存在争议。

items.en: The family goes back to PIE *mei- (2) 'small', the root also behind minus, minimum, diminish, minute and minuscule.
items.cn: 这个词族可追溯到原始印欧语 *mei-（第二支）“小”，该词根也是 minus、minimum、diminish、minute、minuscule 的来源。

items.en: The general adjectival sense 'lesser or smaller than the other' is recorded from early 15c.; 'underage' is recorded from the 1570s.
items.cn: 一般形容词义“比另一个更小、更次要”于 15 世纪早期有记录；“未成年的”义于 16 世纪 70 年代有记录。

items.en: From the 1610s the noun means 'a person below legal age'. The musical sense dates from the 1690s, for intervals and keys built on a minor third; chords follow by 1797.
items.cn: 名词从 17 世纪 10 年代起表示“未达法定年龄的人”。音乐义始于 17 世纪 90 年代，指以小三度构成的音程与调；和弦用法到 1797 年才出现。

items.en: Minor league is recorded from 1884, with the figurative extension by 1926. The academic minor is from 1890, and the verb 'to minor in' from 1905.
items.cn: minor league 于 1884 年有记录，其比喻用法到 1926 年出现。学业上的“辅修”始于 1890 年，动词用法“辅修”始于 1905 年。

note.en: The first group separates the sound-alike miner, the derived noun minority and the superlative neighbour minimum. The second group compares minor with small, lesser, its opposite major, and slight.
note.cn: 第一组区分同音的 miner、派生名词 minority 和最高级邻词 minimum；第二组把 minor 与 small、lesser、它的反义 major 以及 slight 作比较。

entries.definition: a person who works in a mine. It sounds almost the same as minor but comes from mine, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 在矿里工作的人。它与 minor 读音几乎相同，却来自 mine 这条不同的词根。

entries.definition: a smaller group, or the state of being under legal age. It is the noun built on minor, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 少数群体，或未成年状态。它是建立在 minor 之上的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: the smallest amount possible. It comes from minimus, the superlative that sits above minor on the same Latin scale.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小量。它来自 minimus，即同一把拉丁尺子上高于 minor 的最高级。

entries.definition: a musical key built on a minor third. It is a fixed compound using the adjective, not a separate root word or a legal term.
entries.definitionCN: 以小三级构成的小调。它是使用这个形容词的固定复合词，不是另一个词根词，也不是法律用语。

entries.definition: little in size or amount. It is a plain description with no comparison built in, while minor always implies a partner it is measured against.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量小。它是没有内置比较的平实描述，而 minor 总暗示着一个被拿来对照的伙伴。

entries.definition: smaller in importance or degree. It is a formal comparative close to minor, but it cannot mean 'underage' or name a musical key.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或程度上更小。它是接近 minor 的正式比较级，但不能表示“未成年”，也不能指音乐调性。

entries.definition: greater or more important. It is the direct opposite of minor in rank, in music, in sport and in academic study.
entries.definitionCN: 更大的；更重要的。它在等级、音乐、体育和学业上都是 minor 的直接对立面。

entries.definition: small in degree and often unimportant. It overlaps minor in the 'not serious' sense, but cannot carry the ranking or legal senses.
entries.definitionCN: 程度小，常不重要。它在“不严重”这一义项上与 minor 重叠，却不能承载等级或法律义。

normalIntro.en: Real grammar and real relatives: minor is already a Latin comparative, major is its opposite, minority and minimum share the same smallness root.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实语法与真实同族词：minor 本身就是拉丁比较级，major 是它的反面，minority 与 minimum 共享同一条“小”的词根。

normal.en: Minor is already a comparative in Latin, 'smaller'. English does not add -er to it, so there is no 'minorer'.
normal.cn: minor 在拉丁语里已经是比较级“更小的”。英语不再给它加 -er，所以不存在“minorer”这种形式。

normal.en: Major and minor are a pair: Latin maior and minor, both comparatives, one from magnus and one from the *mei- family.
normal.cn: major 与 minor 是一对：拉丁语 maior 与 minor 都是比较级，一个出自 magnus，一个出自 *mei- 词族。

normal.en: Minor key: the third is shorter than the major third, so the interval itself is literally minor.
normal.cn: 小调：它的三度比大三度短，所以这个音程本身就是“较小的”。

normal.en: A college minor is the smaller half of a double subject: fewer credits than the major.
normal.cn: 大学的辅修是双主修里较小的那一半：学分比主修少。

normal.en: Minor league teams sit below the major league; the word keeps the same 'lesser' ranking.
normal.cn: 小联盟球队坐在大联盟下面一级；这个词保留着同一个“次一等”的排名含义。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with two pans. Minor is not the pan that is empty; it is the pan that is lighter than the one opposite it.
abstract.cn: 想象一架有两只盘的天平。minor 不是空着的那只盘，而是比对面那只更轻的盘。

abstract.en: Minor does not mean tiny. It means smaller than the thing it is compared with, so a minor injury can still hurt.
abstract.cn: minor 不等于“极小”。它表示比对照物更小，所以轻伤也仍然会疼。

abstract.en: The same ranking word moves between size, importance, age and music: in each case something sits one step below its partner.
abstract.cn: 同一个表示排位的词在尺寸、重要性、年龄和音乐之间移动：每一种情形里，都有某物比它的伙伴低一级。

examples.en: The road was closed after a minor collision.
examples.cn: 一起小碰撞之后，这条路被封了。

examples.en: She majored in biology with a minor in statistics.
examples.cn: 她主修生物学，辅修统计学。

examples.en: The film's minor characters are more memorable than its hero.
examples.cn: 这部电影的次要角色比主角更令人难忘。

dict_mnemonic.text: “买呢”——买呢子大衣时只剩小一号的，只好买了那件小号的 → minor 较小的、次要的

root: 源自拉丁语 minor“更小的、更少的、更年幼的”，是 minus 一系的比较级，核心是“同一对里较轻的那一端”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of minor, all from one position: the lighter pan of a balance, the member of a pair that is smaller, lower, younger, or less important than its partner.
sensesIntro.cn: minor 的九个义项都来自同一个位置：天平上较轻的那只盘，也就是一对事物中比伙伴更小、更低、更年幼或更不重要的那一个。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the lighter pan of a balance, always weighed against a heavier partner.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上较轻的那只盘，永远与更重的伙伴一起被衡量。

branches.en: SIZE AND DEGREE: the shorter of two paired things, or a degree too small to count as serious.
branches.cn: 尺寸与程度：一对事物中较短的那一个，或小到不算严重的程度。

branches.en: RANK: a lesser role in a negotiation, and the leagues that sit below the major ones.
branches.cn: 等级：谈判中较次要的角色，以及坐在大联盟下面一级的联赛。

branches.en: AGE: the adjective and the noun both mark a person below the legal line of full adult rights.
branches.cn: 年龄：形容词与名词都标记处于完整成年权利线以下的人。

branches.en: MUSIC: a third shorter than the major third gives the minor key its name.
branches.cn: 音乐：比大三度短的三度，给了小调这个名字。

branches.en: FORMAL SUBSYSTEMS: the minor premise and the secondary subject are each the lesser member of a pair.
branches.cn: 形式化的子系统：小前提与辅修科目，各自都是一对中的较小成员。

intro.en: Minor is not built with an English affix; it is a Latin comparative borrowed whole. Its family grows through -ity, through compounds such as minor league and minor key, and through the related *mei- root.
intro.cn: minor 不是用英语词缀构成的，而是整体借入的拉丁比较级。它的词族通过 -ity、通过 minor league 与 minor key 这类复合词，以及通过相关的 *mei- 词根扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin minor, minus and minimus belong to one scale: minor 'smaller', minus 'less', minimus 'smallest'. Parvus 'small' is traditionally paired with them in grammar, but it is a different root, so the relation is suppletive rather than derivational.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minor、minus、minimus 属于同一把尺子：minor“更小”、minus“更少”、minimus“最小”。parvus“小”在语法传统上与它们配成一组，但它是另一条词根，因此这是异根补充关系，而不是派生关系。

items.structure: Latin minor, comparative of the *mei- family
items.meaningCN: 更小的；较次要的；较年幼的（拉丁语比较级）
items.example: The minor road joins the highway two miles north.
items.exampleCN: 那条小路在往北两英里处接入高速公路。

items.meaning: a smaller group; the state of being under age
items.meaningCN: 少数群体；未成年状态（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The proposal was supported by only a small minority.
items.exampleCN: 这项提案只得到一小部分人的支持。

items.meaning: a sports league below the top professional level
items.meaningCN: 低于顶级职业水平的体育联赛（复合名词）
items.example: He played five years in the minor leagues.

items.meaning: a musical key built on a minor third
items.meaningCN: 以小三级构成的小调（复合名词）
items.example: The scene is scored in a slow minor key.
items.exampleCN: 这一幕配的是缓慢的小调。

items.meaningCN: 最小量；最低限度（minimus 的中性形式）
items.example: Keep the temperature at a minimum of ten degrees.
items.exampleCN: 把温度保持在至少十度。

items.meaning: to reduce to the smallest amount
items.meaningCN: 使最小化；把……降到最低（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The new route minimizes travel time.
items.exampleCN: 新路线把行程时间减到最少。

items.meaning: less; the subtraction sign; a drawback
items.meaningCN: 减去；负号；不利因素（minor 的中性形式）
items.example: The plan has one clear minus: it is expensive.
items.exampleCN: 这个方案有一个明显的短板：它很贵。

items.meaningCN: 减少；削弱（di- 离开 + minuere 减少）
items.example: Interest in the case diminished over the years.
items.exampleCN: 这些年，人们对这桩案子的兴趣减弱了。

items.meaningCN: 极小的（作形容词，来自拉丁语 minutus“小的”）
items.example: The differences between the two samples are minute.
items.exampleCN: 两个样本之间的差异极其微小。

items.meaning: a person who serves in a government or church
items.meaningCN: 部长；大臣；牧师（拉丁语 minister“仆人”，源自 minus）
items.example: The foreign minister signed the agreement.
items.exampleCN: 外交部长签署了这项协议。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 更小的；较少的；较年幼的

latinEntries.structure: neuter of minor, used as a noun and preposition
